News.title: Sick tactics of Thai mafia with £200 hitmen, £11 grenades & girls sold into sex trade by dads…as innocent Brits targeted
News.content:
IT’S known as the “land of smiles” with more than a million Brits visiting Thailand every year.

But a dark cloud hangs over the backpacker destination as crime gangs target tourists in cheap cons and the country is dogged by claims of mafia rule.



The Sun can today reveal the truth behind the Thai gangs who carry out £200 hits on mopeds, sell hand grenades for £11 and encourage poverty-stricken families to sell their daughters into the sex trade.

One Brit claimed he was tricked out of £100,000 and suffered sinister threats after setting up business in the Asian country while an ex-drug smuggler lifted the lid on how weapons stolen from military and police armouries are sold on the streets for a few hundred pounds.

Thailand has long denied it has a criminal gang problem but rumours of the Thai mafia first drew attention back in 2014 when the disfigured bodies of British backpackers David Miller, 24, and Hannah Witheridge, 23, were discovered on party island Koh Tao.



At the time, local police insisted there was “100 per cent” no mafia, yet plans to raid “influential rackets and illegitimate businesses” were announced.

But David’s terrified pal Sean McAnna, then 25, claimed the “Thai mafia are trying to kill me” after unknowingly meeting mobsters in a bar, who tried to pressure him to take the rap for the murders and threatened: “You die tonight.”

Sean, a Scottish busker, fled from the islands fearing for his life. And since that terrifying incident more crimes linked to organised crime groups have emerged.

When local taxi driver Sikharin Promcharoen, 31, was beaten-up and fatally shot six times in June, after dropping off tourists on a popular strip in Koh Samui, it was suspected to be linked to the ‘Samui taxi mafia’.

The alleged killer, alongside 11 other suspects, have since been arrested and Sikharin’s family fled the island fearing ‘mafia’ retribution after receiving suspicious calls asking about their whereabouts. Police say the shooting followed a personal dispute.



Now yet another mafia crackdown has since been announced by Thai authorities after they received reports of a series of safety incidents and assaults on foreign tourists at well-known holiday islands.

Officials have also warned any state officials involved, turning a blind eye or facilitating offenders, would face “legal action to the fullest extent”.

One man who knows Thailand’s crooked underworld all too well is Jonathan Wheeler, now 65, and living in Southampton, after spending 18 years in prison for trying to smuggle 4lb of heroin out of the country.

“Thailand’s mafia is not like the Sicilian mafia, they are smaller, family mafia groups and are especially prominent on the islands,” Jonathan, who wrote memoir The Tiger Cage: 18 Years In Thai Prison, tells The Sun.

“They deal in drugs, extortion, protection rackets, prostitution, it’s all there. Some work with the triad groups, like 14k, who are a more organised crime group and move drug shipments and buy and sell women for sex – many of whom are virgins.”



Prior to his incarceration in 1994, Jonathan mingled among dangerous figures while coaching and fighting in Thai boxing competitions and narrowly dodged two assassination attempts from mafia groups.

He says killings are mainly carried out by ‘motorcycle hitmen’, who were “10 a penny” and paid as little as £200 to take someone out.

Their targets were typically rival mafia gang members and drug dealers who had encroached on another group’s turf or had an unpaid debt.

“Some killings are arranged from burner phones in prison and paid for with money or a kilo of crystal meth,” Jonathan says. “If someone owes a debt, they will just shoot them, take over their contacts and begin distribution.”

Nipping around on unrestricted 150CC motorbikes and scooters, meaning they accelerate quicker, Jonathan says they are “much faster than a 2,000CC bike”.



Handguns are the weapon of choice for them, he claims. They ride up, shoot and escape by weaving through traffic at speed and then throw away the weapon.

Jonathan claims that, in Thailand, weapons are “more easily accessible than in America”, with handguns being flogged for £330, M16 assault rifles for £500 and grenades for £11.

Some of the weapons are nicked from military and police armouries to sell on, he alleges.



In the last five years, Thai officers have seized at least 51 assault rifles stolen from their arsenals. And back in May, two M16 rifles, 790 rounds of ammo, grenades, mines and nearly 5kg of explosives were retrieved after being sold to crime groups.

Jonathan narrowly escaped two assassination attempts, once he was nearly rammed off the road for selling hashish on someone else’s patch.

The other happened in Koh Samui after he objected to 22kilos of weed, stashed inside four bin-liners, being stored in a bungalow he was staying at.

“I said, ‘Get the f*** out’, which he did,” he recalls. “He put it in another bungalow. Because I was a witness to it they didn’t want the truth coming out and sent a little guy to come kill me.

“Fortunately, I was sober. It was 3am outside a bar. I saw him walk out of the shadows and pull a revolver out of his jacket.”



He managed to draw attention to the shooter, stopping him in his tracks.

Jonathan describes the Thai mafia gangs as “fearless” because all carry guns, adding: “Even if you’re a champion fighter, they don’t give a f*** because they can just shoot you.”

Some of the killers are especially violent. One mafia member boasted to Jonathan about his bloodthirsty payback after being badly beaten-up by three men.

Jonathan continues: “He caught two of them, grabbing them by the hair and shooting them in the head. It was a brutal revenge.

“He claimed to have paid the police 100,000baht (£2.2k) to make the problem go away. That was the late ’80s, he told me he could help with any problem other than drugs.”



Jonathan also recalls seeing the “No1 mafia boss” of Koh Samui, a man in his 70s, who always had two women in their 40s on his arm and drove around in an old buggy.

Another time, he recalled seeing another mafia man on a motorbike with a cigarette hanging out his mouth, when he hit a police officer “knocking him out”.

“Nothing happened because the mafia guy paid him off,” he says. “To be able to punch a policeman you have to be very powerful.”



Another of the Thai mafia’s trades is sex work. He claims poor families in the north-east are targeted and women go from “picking rice in a field to dancing on a pole and prostitution”.

“Some are happy to loan their daughters for a year in exchange for a motorbike or a scooter, which costs around £800,” Jonathan says.

“Most of these girls have never worn a g-string or a bra in their life before. They are available for sex and often will stay with men for multiple days at a time.”

Jonathan claims that if the sex worker has a brother who is working for the gang, he “will always push her to charge more”.

In addition to those trades, he says many operate extortion and protection rackets and some “higher-ups” rent out bungalows to rich tourists “with everything they want, including drugs”.



Many of the most dangerous aspects, which Thai police have continued to crack down upon, will go unnoticed by tourists – but there are still pitfalls to be wary of.

“For tourists, they just try to rinse them for what they can – whether it’s charging more to reach islands by boat, taxis, tuk-tuks or selling the whole spectrum including drugs,” Jonathan says.

Luke, not his real name, who has spent three years living in Thailand, tells us “there’s a scammer on every corner” waiting to con tourists out of cash.

He says: “It could be fake police, criminals posing as officers, to fine drunken tourists or vendors renting out faulty jet skis that break down leaving you liable to pay for ‘repairs.’”

Another scam he recalled was drivers on taxi apps, like Bolt or Grab, cancelling their job and asking riders to pay in cash – only upon arrival to demand a rate as much as 10 times higher.



Brits who emigrate to Thailand face similar difficulties, according to Rich Mason, 45, from Leicestershire, who claims he was conned out of £100,000 after investing in a business and is now reliant on GoFundMe donations.

He bought shares in gym firm Legacy Muscle Universe Company Limited only for the Thai owners to refuse to pay out dividends, block his phone number and try to get him deported to evade payment.

“The whole thing was just a lie,” Rich tells us. “They even tried to bribe my girlfriend to turn on me and file a fake police report to get me deported to prevent them having to pay me.



“She told me right away. I called them and shouted, ‘What the f*** are you playing at?’ and they hung up. They blocked me on everything soon after.”

He says they claimed to be part of the Thai mafia, threatening him and also pals, telling them: “He die, he die. If I see him, I kill him.”

Rich adds: “He made a lot of threats and tried bully boy and scare tactics, even telling my girlfriend if I came back I’d be in ‘big trouble.’”

His situation worsened when he was near-fatally runover in March, which “smashed my leg to pieces”. He suffered broken feet, pneumonia and blood clots in his lung and leg.

Rich says: “I was left for dead, I died twice and think they were hoping it would be my end so they could take my money. That’s how ruthless they are.



“As a foreigner living in Thailand, you have minimal to zero rights, so you can get scammed and there’s not much you can do about it.

“Don’t invest or build any business unless you have a lot of money, very good legal representation and are 100 per cent sure about it.”

When contacted by The Sun, the owners of Legacy Muscle Universe denied Rich’s claims, insisting he will be paid on the one year anniversary of his investment. Rich argues this wasn’t their agreement and currently, no money has materialised.

In spite of his troubles, Rich, who is still recovering in Thailand and is reliant on donations due to having no financial support, doesn’t dissuade others from visiting.

But he has a strong warning, telling us: “Before everything that happened, I thought of Thailand as this dream paradise that was magical.



“But if you live here, you’re in a very unstable position. You don’t have the same rights as Thai people and that dream of Thailand doesn’t last forever.”

The Sun contacted the Royal Thai Government and Royal Thai Police but did not receive a response. The Tourism Authority of Thailand applauded The Sun for “shedding light on this issue” but was unable to comment further.

Jonathan Wheeler’s memoir The Tiger Cage: 18 Years In Thai Prison – about his years among the Thai mafia and subsequent imprisonment for drug smuggling – is available to buy here.

News.title: Man in hospital after being ‘attacked and sexually assaulted’ in town centre in the early hours
News.content:
HORROR 'ASSAULT' Man in hospital after being ‘attacked and sexually assaulted’ in town centre in the early hours

A MAN has been rushed to hospital after he was allegedly attacked and sexually assaulted in a town centre in the early hours.

The reported incident unfolded in Macclesfield, Cheshire, at around 1am on Tuesday.

Police were called to the scene on Churchill Way after receiving reports that a man had been assaulted and sexually assaulted.

The victim was taken to hospital in an ambulance where he remains at this time.





Cheshire Constabulary is appealing for anyone with any information that may assist their probe into the horror to come forward.

The force is also asking for anyone with dashcam footage or any witnesses to contact police immediately.

DI Claire Miles said: “An investigation is currently ongoing, and we would like to hear from anyone who may have witnessed the incident or saw anything suspicious or relevant in the area before or after it is believed to have occurred.

“We would also ask anyone who was driving in Macclesfield town centre between 10.40pm on Monday 10 August and 1.10am on Tuesday 11 August, to please check their dashcam footage to see if anything relevant has been captured.

“This includes near to the Churchill Way and Sunderland Street area.

“Anyone with any concerns, or to report any information, should contact Cheshire Police on 101 or report online, quoting IML-2393346.”

News.title: Brit flight to Spain catches stunning moment solar eclipse blackens sky mid-air as pilot warns passengers about looking
News.content:
THIS is the incredible moment travellers on a flight from the UK to Spain caught a stunning solar eclipse in mid-air.

The footage, which was filmed by a passenger on flight BA2644 from Gatwick to Malaga, saw the once-in-a-lifetime celestial event happening while thousands of feet in the air.



Passengers were left in awe as they caught a glimpse of the best solar eclipse in almost three decades.

The video shows how the moon had slowly edged in front of sun, blocking it out in a perfect circle to provide a memory those on the flight would never forget.



Hundreds of lucky passengers on the flight managed to watch the unique moment from a front-row seat above the clouds.

The pilot could be heard warning passengers about exercising caution while looking and not to stare directly.



Passengers could not hold back their excitement as they could be heard murmuring and gasping as they watched the rare phenomenon unfold before their eyes.

In parts of Spain as well as Iceland and Greenland, the sun was completely covered by the moon – known as totality.

And the stunning footage which reflected this phenomenon was captured not far from the Bay of Biscay near northern Spain.

The path of totality was at its strongest in this region, according to astronomers.



Today’s solar eclipse will be the first total solar eclipse visible from the Iberian Peninsula since 1912.

It comes as thousands of Brits back home gathered at viewpoints across the UK, including beaches and parks to witness the incredible celestial event.

Up to 95 per cent of the Sun was obscured by the moon in certain parts of the country as the eclipse peaked.



Brits heeded advice to avoid staring directly at the spectacle with millions turning out wearing sun-safe ­goggles to watch the stellar event.

Others armed themselves with colanders, cardboard contraptions and even welding masks.

In cities, crowds took to parks and rooftops as the eclipse brought traffic to a stop while birds ceased singing.

Witnesses who joined the Bristol Astronomical Society on the Avon Gorge described an eerie feeling as the temperature cooled and the sky went dark.

Sadly, not all parts of the UK got to see a clear view of the eclipse.



Lots of views in Scotland and other parts of the country were blocked by clouds, though much of England enjoyed bright clear skies.

Countryside residents got the most dramatic effect thanks to minimal light pollution.

Parts of northern England missed out because of cloud cover.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

And in Belfast, people marvelled at the eclipse as it shone bright through dark clouds.

The next time the sun will be obscured so much in the UK will be 2081.

News.title: Two dead after military helicopter crashes in Texas as smash sparks wildfire & officials launch probe
News.content:
TWO pilots have been killed in a military helicopter crash after the chopper slammed into a field and burst into flames.

The deadly crash sparked a huge wildfire in Texas as dry grass quickly caught light, with firefighters battling the blaze for hours.



AH-64 Apache attack helicopter was based at the nearby US Army base of Fort Hood, the military said.

It crashed near the village of Salado, around 60miles north of Austin.





Emergency responders arrived to a huge blaze engulfing the chopper.

Officers had rushed to the scene at around 1.33pm after receiving reports about the wreckage.

Two minutes later, both pilots onboard were declared dead.

Bell County Sheriff’s Office spokesman Cliff Coleman said when they arrived the huge fire was already “getting out of control very quickly”.



He confirmed the chopper did not hit any structures or people as it fell out of the sky.

Coleman told reporters: “It crashed into a field, you could tell it was a violent crash.”

Dramatic photos showed the wreckage smoking as debris burnt in the dry grass.



A huge wildfire was sparked by the horror crash as the grass ignited, forcing locals to evacuate their homes.

The blaze tore through around 100 acres of land and took several hours to get under control.

Several local roads were closed as the inferno raged.

Acting commanding general at Fort Hood Brig. Gen. Ethan Diven told local news: “Our immediate priority is securing the site and supporting the initial response efforts.

“Our thoughts are with the crew and their families as we await further information.”



Texas Governor Greg Abbott wrote on X: “Today, an Apache helicopter crashed in Bell County during Fort Hood operations, killing two members of our military.

“Join Cecilia and me in prayer for their families and the entire Fort Hood community. Texas is forever indebted to those who serve our state and nation,” the governor said in the post.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The identities of the pilots have not yet been released.

Officials launched an investigation into the accident.

News.title: Luxury villa used in James Bond film where spy says iconic catchphrase has ‘elegant’ apartment go up for sale
News.content:

FOR YOUR KEYS ONLY

FOR YOUR KEYS ONLY Luxury villa used in James Bond film where spy says iconic catchphrase has ‘elegant’ apartment go up for sale

AN apartment in the luxurious Italian villa featured in Casino Royale has gone on the market.

The property – where James Bond delivers his iconic catchphrase – sits on the shores of glamorous Lake Como in northern Italy.



In the final scene of the first Bond film starring Daniel Craig, a black Jaguar pulls up the driveway of Villa La Gaeta.

Bond’s nemesis, Mr White, steps out of the car – only for a gunshot to ring out, sending the villain crashing to the ground.



Bond then appears in a full suit, gun in hand, and delivers the iconic line: “The name’s Bond, James Bond.”

Since the film’s release, the villa has become a magnet for Bond fans from around the world.

Until now, those wanting to experience the property could rent it for around €520 a night.

But an apartment inside the iconic villa is now being offered for sale by luxury property firm Sotheby’s International Realty.



The apartment features five rooms on the ground floor, with two bedrooms, a study and two bathrooms spread across two levels.

It also comes with two basement storage rooms and parking spaces.

“This property promises truly elegant living on Lake Como,” the estate agent told BILD.

Built in 1921 to designs by brothers Gino and Adolfo Coppedè, the property has a monthly maintenance fee of €400.

“As the owners, you don’t have to worry about anything on the property; a caretaker looks after the garden and the boat dock,” the listing says.



The Bond connection isn’t the only luxury on offer.

The south-facing terrace promises a “beautiful lake view” in the evening sun, according to the real estate agent.

The new owner will also have direct access to Lake Como, including a private beach.

There are boat berths in the villa’s private marina, a jetty and a swimming pool.

To sweeten the deal further, the complex is surrounded by sprawling parkland filled with “exotic and rare plants”.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

According to Sotheby’s, the apartment was renovated in 2023.

Anyone hoping to make this slice of Bond history their own will need to find €1.45 million.

News.title: ‘Afghan migrants pinned woman down’ and ‘raped her at knifepoint in sex attack’ at London park
News.content:
Add us as a preferred source

PARK HORROR ‘Afghan migrants pinned woman down’ and ‘raped her at knifepoint in sex attack’ at London park

A WOMAN broke down in tears after allegedly being raped at knifepoint by two “Afghan males” in a London park, a court heard.

The victim was spending time with a male friend in Barking Park in East London on August 16, 2025.

The woman and her friend were then approached by Noorullah Ahmdzai, 26, and a co-defendant teenage boy, whose identity cannot be reported for legal reasons, the court heard.

Snaresbrook Crown Court heard that the pair pinned the woman to the ground before threatening her and her friend with a knife.





Giving evidence, the woman described one of her alleged attackers as having “a beard, not like a big one, a small one”.

She told the court: “He was talking in an accent, like people from Afghanistan talk. He pulled [my trousers] down.

“He was trying to kiss me.”

The woman then alleged that both men proceeded to rape her.

Proceedings were briefly adjourned after she broke down during cross-examination by Ahmdzai’s barrister, Emily Culverhouse.

Ms Culverhouse put to the witness: “There was an agreement that you would have sex with both men for £70?”

“No, that is not true,” the woman replied, telling the court she had been forcibly restrained.

She added: “One of them was pushing me against the ground so that I can’t move, and the other person was on me.



“One of them was grabbing my legs.

“I don’t remember who tried to kiss me but one of them tried to kiss me.”

When the barrister alleged, “You complained because you wanted £500,” the woman answered, “No.”

Ms Culverhouse further pressed: “You said that you would call the police and make things bad for them?”

Ahmdzai, of Barking, east London, and his teenage co-defendant both deny rape, threatening another with a blade or point, and false imprisonment.



The teenager additionally denies assault by penetration.

The trial continues.

News.title: Moment Russian air defences desperately try to shoot down Ukraine attack as drones and missiles blitz Putin’s warships
News.content:
THIS is the shocking moment Russian air defences scramble to repel a Ukrainian blitz targeting the key Black Sea port of Novorossiysk.

Dramatic footage shows the night sky erupting as missiles streak upwards from Russian air-defence systems.



In separate footage, concerned witnesses gather around as smoke billows from the smouldering wreckage.

A third clip shows a water cannon battling to extinguish flames, while a line of cars backs up in the foreground.



The major attack on Novorossiysk destroyed warships and forced two major grain terminals to suspend operations.

Regional Governor Veniamin Kondratyev said at least two people were killed, including an eight-year-old girl.

Ukraine‘s SBU security service described the assault as being of “strategic significance”, saying the naval base was struck by a barrage of drones and missiles.

Volodymyr Zelenskyy said two frigates, a large landing ship, a corvette and other vessels were hit.



The strikes have also raised fears of disruption to global food supplies, with Russia among the world’s largest wheat exporters.

Russia’s Agriculture Ministry said it was working to establish alternative routes for exports.

One of the country’s main grain lobby groups warned last month that further attacks could shut down Black Sea grain exports entirely, potentially sending prices soaring.

Novorossiysk Mayor Andrei Kravchenko said the port suspended its water supply and declared a state of emergency following the strikes.

He said four businesses, more than two dozen residential buildings and several educational facilities were damaged.



The attack comes after heavy strikes on Ukrainian grain shipments in the Black Sea.

According to Ukraine’s Agriculture Ministry, shipments fell by 76 per cent in the first two weeks of August compared with the same period last year.

On Wednesday, Ukraine and Moldova also agreed a plan to route Ukrainian grain shipments through Moldova by rail.



Separately, more than three dozen drones were shot down over Sevastopol in Crimea on Wednesday.

As the bitter conflict enters its fifth year, Moscow has intensified strikes on Ukrainian logistics and warehouse facilities in response to attacks by Kyiv.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Zelensky said on Tuesday that Ukraine had handed US negotiators proposals for a plan to end the conflict.

Kyiv has repeatedly called for a ceasefire, while Moscow maintains that any settlement must involve Ukraine relinquishing territory.

News.title: Chancellor John Healey warned by voters to keep fuel duty freeze in place as pump prices soar
News.content:
VOTERS have warned Chancellor John Healey to keep the fuel duty freeze in place as prices soar.

Sixty-three per cent of Brits demand the rate be kept down as motorists grapple with high pump prices amid the Middle East conflict.



Pressure will mount on the Treasury in the run up to the Budget to maintain the freeze following The Sun’s 15-year campaign to help motorists.

Mr Healey also faces calls to extend the temporary 5p duty that is due to expire at the end of December.



Government documents say they will confirm the final rates at the Budget at the end of October.

A breakdown of the figures show 31 per cent strongly support a fuel duty freeze at its current rate with 32 per cent saying they somwhat support keeping the rate as it is.

Separately, 55 per cent say fuel duty should be reduced with 24 per cent say it should stay as it is.

Ex-Chancellor Rachel Reeves abandoned plans to hike fuel duty by 5p back in May in the aftermath of the Iran war.

Petrol hit 161.66p over the weekend as diesel has rocketed by 17p in a month now standing at 182p per litre.

A litre of petrol cost just 132.83p on the day the conflict broke out, while diesel cost 142.38p a litre.



Simon Williams, from the RAC, said: “The price of petrol appears to have finally reached an Iran War peak, having risen 11p over 33 consecutive days.

“While prices should fall a little in the coming days, this may be short-lived as the cost of a barrel of oil has climbed almost $10 in the last week towards $90.

“The current situation shows just how volatile fuel prices are and how drivers in the UK are at the mercy of global events.”

News.title: Saddleworth Moor fire LIVE: Emergency crews battle huge moorland blaze as road closed
News.content:
The blaze has broken out at Saddleworth Moor in Greater Manchester

Residents have been told to avoid the area on Thursday morning - fire crews have been tackling the huge fire which has broken out in Oldham throughout the night

Firefighters are tackling a massive blaze in Greater Manchester which has seen a blaze engulf a huge area of moorland.

In a statement issued on Thursday, a spokesperson for Greater Manchester Fire and Rescue Service confirmed: "Our crews have been tackling a moorland fire near Holmfirth Road in Oldham through the night.

"Please avoid the area while emergency services respond to the incident."

The blaze at Saddleworth Moor comes after wildfires have ravaged Greater Manchester and sections of the UK over the summer. Major blazes erupted at Dovestone and Tintwistle earlier this summer, with the fires damaging nearly 1,000 acres of land.

News.title: A-Level results LIVE: Students face anxious wait for 2026 exam grades at 8am
News.content:
Hundreds and thousands of students will get their A-Level results today

Hundreds of thousands of students across the UK are set to receive their A-level and BTec results this morning as the cost of university remains in the spotlight

Hundreds of thousands of students in England, Wales and Northern Ireland will receive their A-Level, BTec and T-level results this morning.

Most schools and colleges are set to open their doors at 8am on Thursday, August 13 for students to pick up their physical results slips, however students may already be able to view their university application status via an online portal prior to this.

It is expected that a record number of students will find out if they have secured their first choice of university this year as by the end of June around 41% of UK 18-year-olds had applied to university.

As the results come in and the cost of universities has been in the spotlight, the chief of Universities UK, which represents more than 140 vice-chancellors, urged pupils to not "let politicians make your decision for you".

Last year, the proportion of students getting top A-level results reached a record high, with schools likely facing pressure to continue to produce these outcomes.

In 2025 28.3% of all grades across England, Wales and Northern Ireland came in at A* or A.

Follow our live blog for further updates as results day takes place.

News.title: Urgent recall issued for 13,500kg of beef products - full list
News.content:
Urgent recall issued for 13,500kg of beef products - full list

The products were produced between May 15 and May 20 and have use-or-freeze-by dates from between September 15 and September 20, according to the US Department of Agriculture

View 3 Images Some raw beef products have been recalled [stock image] (Image: Getty)

The US has recalled raw beef products imported from Argentina to America after the products failed inspection.

‌



The recall by the US Department of Agriculture affects 29,628 pounds (around 13,440kg) of raw beef products that were distributed in two states by Corte Argentino USA LLC.

‌



The USDA's Food Safety and Inspection Services said in a release that the products - dispatched in Florida and Texas - are listed under the brand FrigorIfico Gorina SAIC.

‌



They were distributed to retailers without the required federal import reinspection.

View 3 Images The recall was issued by the US Department of Agriculture (Image: Getty)

The reinspection process certifies that labelling, documentation and a product's condition abide by federal guidelines.

‌



The products were produced between May 15 and May 20.

They have use-or-freeze-by dates from between September 15 and September 20.

The recalled products include:

‌



FrigorIfico Gorina SAIC boneless beef "Top Sirloin Butt"

FrigorIfico Gorina SAIC boneless beef "Eye Round"

FrigorIfico Gorina SAIC boneless beef "Topside Cap Off"

FrigorIfico Gorina SAIC boneless beef "Flat"

FrigorIfico Gorina SAIC boneless beef "Knuckle"

View 3 Images No illness have been reported as a result of consuming the products (Image: Getty)

No illness has been reported as a result of consuming these products.

Article continues below

Consumers who have purchased any recalled beef should immediately dispose of the product.

News.title: Brits stuck in Sicily after Mount Etna eruption ash cloud grounds flights
News.content:
Brits stuck in Sicily after Mount Etna eruption ash cloud grounds flights

Evgenia Filimianova from London, flew to Sicily to attend a friend's wedding with her husband but the pair now "feel like there is no way out" after a huge ash cloud from Mount Etna grounded flights

View 4 Images Evgenia Filimianova is stuck in Sicily (Image: Evgenia Filimianova / SWNS)

A British couple are stranded in Sicily after a huge ash cloud from Mount Etna's eruption grounded flights out of the island.

‌



Mount Etna - the most active volcano in Europe - has erupted multiple times throughout July and August. On August 7, Evgenia Filimianova, 39, from London, flew from Athens to Catania, Sicily, to attend a friend's wedding in Taormina with her husband.

‌



Little did they know, they were one of the last flight's from Athens allowed to land at Catania Airport - the biggest airport on the island.

‌



View 4 Images Mount Etna's eruptive phase persists (Image: Anadolu via Getty Images)

Teenager dead and 211 people evacuated from ferry fire in Bali as five still missing READ MORE :

After travelling to Catania Airport for their flight back home on August 11, they found out their flight was cancelled thirty minutes before it was set to depart.

The couple, who live in London but are staying in Athens for August, are still stranded in Sicily, trying to find their way back home. Meanwhile their seven-year-old daughter is stuck with family in Athens.

‌



"We were having a very nice day in Taormina, at the wedding, enjoying our time there, but we could see the eruption and the volcano spewing lava," Evgenia, a journalist, said.

"Our daughter is in Athens. We have to get back to her."

When Evgenia and her husband first landed in Sicily, they watched Mount Etna erupting from the wedding venue in Taormina.

‌



"It's an incredible thing to be able to witness," she said.

"I've never seen anything like that before I wasn't necessarily scared, but it was concerning. I was just in awe.

"The locals seemed very chill. And we didn't get any emergency texts or direction from the people at the hotel, so we weren't too worried. But then I started reading about travel. As soon as there is ash, the airports start closing."

‌



View 4 Images Disruptions at Catania Airport Due to Mount Etna Eruption (Image: Davide Anastasi/LaPresse/Shutterstock)

Evgenia and her husband stayed in Taormina until they travelled to Catania for their flight back home which was scheduled for August 11.

"We arrived at Catania airport and there were loads and loads of people there," she said.

‌



"There were people sleeping on the floor, families stuck, just lots of people all trying to get out. We waited for our flight, and then 30 minutes before we were meant to depart, it was cancelled and rescheduled for the next day."

Evgenia and her husband spent the night in a hotel, hoping to fly without problem the next day. But on August 12, Catania Airport announced there would be no arrivals or departures due to the ash cloud above the island.

"It feels like there is no way out," she said.

‌



"The buses and trains are fully booked, the airports are closed, the taxis are too expensive, the hotels are getting booked up. Every option to travel is already taken by someone else.

"My daughter is staying with family in Athens, we have to get back to her. She's upset, like any child would be, and so are we. She's in good hands, but this was not the plan."

View 4 Images A huge ash cloud from Mount Etna's eruption grounded flights out of the island (Image: Evgenia Filimianova / SWNS)

‌



The couple are now planning to get to Malta and then make their way back to Athens from there.

"The plan is to get a cab to the bus station, then a three hour bus to Porto di Pozzallo, then a ferry to Malta, then a cab to a hotel, stay there overnight and then a cab to the airport.

"And then we're just hoping we'll be able to fly to Athens."

‌



The couple have already spent a huge amount of money on emergency travel and accommodation.

"We must have already spent at least £1,000. And we don't even know if our insurance will pay out," she said.

"Emotionally, it's not easy. It's stressful and tiring and we weren't prepared for it. We're acting like 24/7 booking agents. I'm constantly on the phone, constantly figuring out connections and travel."

Article continues below

Currently, Catania Airport has suspended all arrivals and departures until 4pm on August 13, but they have advised everyone to check the local travel advice before making their way to the airport.

Flights are still operating from Palermo Airport on the north of the island, but Evgenia has said that flights from there are fully booked.

News.title: Blood pressure drug urgently recalled due to 'health consequences' risk
News.content:
Blood pressure drug urgently recalled due to 'health consequences' risk

The FDA have urgently recalled a specific batch of blood pressure drugs as they may lead to 'temporary or medically reversible adverse health consequences'

View 2 Images The blood pressure drug has been recalled (Image: Getty Images)

A drug used to treat high blood pressure is being urgently recalled as it could cause 'health consequences'.

‌



The valsartan drug was made by Novartis under the brand name Diovan and has been recalled as it does not meet dissolution specifications.

‌



The drug's effectiveness has therefore been impacted with the potential risk of harmful consequences to anybody who takes it.

‌



View 2 Images The drugs may cause 'health consequences' (Image: Getty)

Diovan is an angiotensin II receptor blocker used to treat hypertension and heart failure.

Patients may also be prescribed the drug after suffering a heart attack.

‌



The US Food and Drug Administration has determined the notice as a Class II recall, which means exposure to the drug may lead to “temporary or medically reversible adverse health consequences.”

The impact is expected to stop once patients stop taking the drug, however they may cause harm and anybody who has their hands on the batch of drugs is urged to chuck them out.

The batch that is being recalled has AV5913C on the packaging and include packages of 90 160-mg tablets with an expiration date of June 2027.

‌



The drug was manufactured by Pantheon Manufacturing Services in Greenville, North Carolina, and distributed by Novartis Pharmaceutical Corp. in Hanover, New Jersey.

The FDA noted that the tablets have been distributed nationwide in the US.

Novartis made the recall on August 4.

‌



The recall comes as the UK is also facing difficulties regarding blood pressure drugs, as the nation faces a 'serious shortage'.

A review carried out by MediWatch on August 4 noted that there is a shortage issue of Ramipril 1.25mg capsules across England, Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland.

A Serious Shortage Protocol was issued by the Department of Health and Social Care (DHSC) on April 22 and then extended to beyond May 29.

Article continues below

This protocol limits community pharmacies to dispensing a maximum of one month's supply per prescription, even for those who usually have prescriptions for two to three months.

News.title: Teenager dead and 211 people evacuated from ferry fire in Bali as five still missing
News.content:
Teenager dead and 211 people evacuated from ferry fire in Bali as five still missing

Five people are still believed to be missing at sea after a ferry fire near the Indonesian tourist island of Bali saw 211 people evacuated and one teenager dead

View 3 Images The National Transportation Safety Committee investigators were determining the cause of the fire. (Image: BASARNAS via AP)

Crews rescued 211 people and recovered the body of a teenage passenger from a ferry that caught fire in rough seas on Wednesday.

‌



The tragic incident happened near the Indonesian tourist island of Bali, authorities said. Videos released by the National Search and Rescue Agency showed people wearing life jackets crowding an inflatable life raft in choppy waters during a rescue operation at sea, as thick black smoke billows from the ferry.

‌



The agency said that as of early Thursday, rescuers evacuated 211 people from the burned vessel, including seven foreign tourists, and recovered the body of a 19-year-old Indonesian woman.

‌



View 3 Images The ferry was transporting 44 vehicles and 53 motorcycles. (Image: BASARNAS via AP)

Five homes completely destroyed as fire rips through residential street in Caerphilly borough READ MORE :

The Putri Yasmin ferry was traveling from Bali to the neighboring island of Lombok in West Nusa Tenggara province when the fire broke out at about 4:15 a.m. Wednesday. The ferry was also transporting 44 vehicles and 53 motorcycles.

The Search and Rescue Office in Mataram, the capital of West Nusa Tenggara province, received an emergency report almost half an hour later and immediately deployed personnel and rescue vessels.

‌



“Our top priority is the safety of all passengers and crew members,” said Muhammad Hariyadi, who heads the Mataram Search and Rescue Office.

The search was continuing Thursday. Relatives who gathered in a post command center in the port reported at least five of their family members still unaccounted for. Their names were posted at the center as missing.

View 3 Images The heat forced some passengers to jump into the sea (Image: BASARNAS via AP)

‌



It is common in Indonesia for the number of passengers to differ from the manifest, but authorities have not said why the number of people evacuated was so much greater. Transportation Minister Dudy Purwagandhi said officials will look into the discrepancy.

“The findings will be thoroughly reviewed as part of the ministry’s evaluation,” Purwagandhi said. “This is a serious issue that will be thoroughly investigated.”

He said the National Transportation Safety Committee investigators were determining the cause of the fire.

‌



Syamsurizal, head of the Lembar Port Authority in Lombok, said that survivors told authorities the blaze appeared to have started in a cargo truck before quickly spreading through the ferry. The heat forced some passengers to jump into the sea, he said.

“The response operation is ongoing, and authorities are continuing to account for all victims,” said Syamsurizal, who like many Indonesians uses a single name. He said at least two injured passengers were rushed to a nearby hospital.

Hariyadi said the rescue effort was supported by six vessels, a helicopter, two inflatable boats and two private yachts. He said rough seas with waves reported as high as 4 meters (13 feet) complicated rescue efforts.

Article continues below

The 62-meter (203-foot) ferry, built in Japan in 1992, can carry up to 220 passengers and 55 vehicles. It is primarily used to transport travelers and cargo between the Indonesian islands of Bali and Lombok, a journey that typically takes four to five hours.

Indonesia is an archipelago of more than 17,000 islands where ferries are a common method of travel. Disasters occur regularly, with weak safety enforcement often blamed.

News.title: Major UK train stations to close for weeks in £70million upgrade
News.content:
Major UK train stations to close for weeks in £70million upgrade

Major projects and will be carried out between September 19 and October 4 - including the completion of a new £70million train station - and there will be some disruption as a result

View 3 Images The Huddersfield and Slaithwaite train stations will close for two weeks (Image: Getty)

Two West Yorkshire train stations will close for weeks to allow for major upgrades.

‌



The Huddersfield and Slaithwaite train stations will close for two weeks from mid-September.

‌



Major projects will be carried out between September 19 and October 4 - including the completion of the new £70million Huddersfield train station.

‌



View 3 Images Huddersfield train station is getting a facelift (Image: Getty Images)

The subway at Huddersfield station will be extended to platforms 4 and 5. These platforms are also getting upgrades to be able to be accommodate longer trains.

The station roof is also getting repaired. A separate, 38-day closure is also planned for later in the year.

‌



The closure will be in place from Christmas Eve to complete Huddersfield station.

The entire project is part of the wider Transpennine Route Upgrade. The upgrade is focused on modernising the railway between Manchester, Huddersfield, Leeds and York.

"While we know there will be some disruption while this work takes place, these upgrades are essential to delivering the more reliable, accessible and higher-capacity railway that customers deserve," said Sophie Leishman, Transpennine Route Upgrade sponsor.

‌



"We're making real progress across the route, from the redevelopment of Huddersfield station to improvements that will support longer trains, better performance and future electrification."

View 3 Images The subway at Huddersfield station will be extended to platforms 4 and 5 (Image: Getty)

Liam O’Shaughnessy, Transpennine Route Upgrade Programme Delivery Lead at Northern, said: "There will be disruption to Northern and other operators’ services during these works, with services amended and some trains replaced with buses.

Article continues below

"We strongly advise all customers to check before they travel and use National Rail Enquiries to plan their journeys."

News.title: How to see 50 shooting stars on Thursday night during Perseid meteor shower - best time
News.content:
How to see 50 shooting stars on Thursday night during Perseid meteor shower - best time

Just hours after the eclipse, a meteor shower peak will begin that is set to delight star-gazers, but the astronomical amazement will continue for days to come

View 2 Images Shooting stars pictured in China a few days ago (Image: VCG, VCG via Getty Images)

Experts have named the best time to witness the Perseid meteor shower set to wow millions after the solar eclipse.

‌



It’s thought to be the first time the peak of a meteor shower has coincided with a solar eclipse, which took place early on Wednesday evening (August 12).

‌



Alfredo Carpineti, space and physics editor at IFL Science and author of the book Invisible Rainbows, said: "It's so exciting to have these two events happening on the same day.

‌



"I've gone through 5,000 years' worth of eclipse data from NASA, and it looks like Wednesday will be the first time there's an eclipse happening on the same day as the peak of a major meteor shower."

The Perseid meteor shower has actually been ongoing for weeks, but its peak starts a few hours after the eclipse. The two-day peak is on Wednesday and Thursday night.

On Wednesday, meteors will be most visible from around midnight until dawn on Thursday. Scientists say the peak of activity will be around 3am on Thursday morning (August 13), when around 100 shooting stars can be seen per hour.

‌



Even if you missed the peak, Thursday night into Friday morning will still be a good time to spot shooting stars, as experts say around 50 will be visible in an hour in dark locations. Usually, the number of meteors drops off by 40-50 percent in the nights following the peak.

However, given the Perseid is one of the most active and reliable meteor showers, there is still a good chance you can spot a shooting star on Thursday night and Friday morning. The Perseids are expected to last until August 24.

View 2 Images The Perseid meteor shower started a couple of weeks ago (Image: Getty/ Gabriel Gonzalez)

‌



The best places to see a meteor shower are in dark countryside or coastal locations, with little light pollution. Star-gazers should look at a 60-degree angle to the sky, wrap up warm, and bring a chair so they don’t injure their neck by holding their head back for long periods of time.

It can take up to 40 minutes for human eyes to adjust to low light, so patience is required — as is vigilance not to check a phone.

Shooting stars occur when pieces of a comet break up as it nears the sun and heats up. The debris ends up in the path of Earth's orbit.

Article continues below

The pieces of the comet are moving through space at the same time Earth is, and when they hit the Earth's atmosphere, smaller pieces are vapourised - leaving bright trails of light we call shooting stars - and larger meteors explode in fireballs, according to the Royal Greenwich Museum.

Those pieces 'slam into our atmosphere at speeds of between 7–45 miles per second', the Museum says, and 'the average speed for a Perseid meteor is 36 miles per second', or a staggering 129,600mph.

News.title: Once-in-a-generation solar eclipse wows millions in UK and Europe
News.content:
The UK and Europe have enjoyed their most dramatic solar eclipse for nearly 30 years, with millions thought to have witnessed the once-in-a-generation event.

Those watching the astronomical phenomenon from the UK were treated to a partial eclipse, which peaked shortly after 19:00 BST, when most saw more than 90% of the Sun covered by the Moon.

But parts of Greenland, Iceland and Spain experienced the complete darkness and spectacle of a total eclipse.

Large crowds at viewing sites across the UK and Europe reacted with gasps and cheers, with astronomy enthusiasts saying it served as a reminder of how "amazing" the Universe is.

News.title: Temperatures to soar to 38C as amber extreme heat warning comes into force
News.content:
A rare amber weather warning for extreme heat will come into effect across a large swathe of the UK on Thursday, with temperatures set to soar as high as 38C (100F).

Thursday will mark the peak of the UK's fifth widespread heatwave this year, with temperatures to be in the mid-30s Celsius across most of the warning area.

Amber heat health alerts, external, which warn of significant impacts to health and social care services, are already in force for the entirety of England until 21:00 BST on Friday.

The searing heat could also lead to power cuts, rail and air travel delays, and cause serious health impacts such as dehydration and heat exhaustion.

News.title: Leading doctor rebukes NHS chiefs over transplants
News.content:
While NHS Blood and Transplant manages organ donations and supports transplant centres, services are commissioned and paid for by NHS England.

But in a letter to NHS England and a small group of patient advocates, Manas said the central body had created a "fragmented" system "with poor accountability".

There is a "mismatch", he said, between each hospital's waiting lists, organ availability, capacity to carry out surgeries and the availability of operating theatres.

This is "leading to last-minute cancellations [and] unpredictable utilisation of donated organs," he warned.

The BBC reported in March that the UK, once a world leader, had fallen behind major Western nations in heart and lung transplantation, though it fares better in other areas such as kidney transplantation.

The NHS transplants one in 10 lungs and one in seven hearts that are donated - half the proportions seen in some other countries.

It has not invested in modern technology at the same rate as other countries, and suffers from a lack of theatre space, intensive care beds and staff.

Wales and Northern Ireland do not have a heart and lung transplant centre, so patients commonly travel to England for surgery. There is one heart transplant centre in Scotland.

News.title: ICE plans to equip agents with gloves that can deliver electric shocks
News.content:
Unlike a taser, which uses sharp barbs in the skin to deliver a shock of up to 50,000 volts, the gloves do not complete an electrical circuit inside the body.

The gloves instead deliver a sharp shock to convince a subject to comply using "pain deterrence", says Lt Butch Gallion, an administrator at Hawkins County jail in Tennessee.

"We may or may not deploy them. It just depends on how they act. When you push the button to turn them on there's a light that displays. The inmates understand that light, and often just seeing the light brings compliance," he says.

The shocks can only be delivered when they contact skin, allowing an officer to touch a subject's clothing, and then move to the skin â typically the wrist or elbow - if they begin to fight.

If they become combative, he continues, "then you can apply the gloves to an area that the skin is exposed. And it's an instant complier for me".

According to the DHS note, GLOVE would be used by officers and agents in Homeland Security Investigations (HSI), which targets transnational criminal organisations, and Enforcement Removal Operations (ERO), which is responsible for arresting, detaining and deporting people who violate immigration laws in the US.

Some law enforcement agencies are already using the gloves but it's believed that the planned ICE purchase would be the largest from Compliant Technologies to date.

Civil rights groups, including the American Civil Liberties Union (ACLU), have expressed alarm about law enforcement using them.

"ICE spent the last year showing this country that they are willing to disregard the law and are too quick to use force, with devastating and at times fatal consequences for citizens and noncitizens alike," said Jenn Rolnick Borchetta, deputy director on policing at the ACLU.

Federal immigration agents have been criticised in the wake of fatalities that have occurred during enforcement operations.

Recent incidents include the fatal shooting of Mexican national Lorenzo Salgado Araujo in Texas, while Colombian national Johan SebastiÃ¡n DurÃ¡n Guerrero was killed during an immigration enforcement operation in Maine.

ICE has also been under pressure to deliver President Donald Trump's deportation agenda, which includes meeting a daily target of arrests.

"Now they [ICE] might be equipped with a device that allows them to deliver an electric shock with their hands by pushing a small button, in a move that might be imperceptible to those watching," Borchetta said.

"Giving immigration agents a concealed means of delivering terrible pain is a recipe for more harm to the public and less accountability."

With reporting by Max Matza

News.title: Major Russian grain export terminals hit in Ukraine Black Sea port attack
News.content:
A "massive" Ukrainian drone and missile strike on Russia's port of Novorossiysk has damaged two major grain export terminals and hit the last big Russian naval base on the Black Sea, reports say.

Three people, including an eight-year-old child, were killed and another 24 injured in the overnight attack, local officials said.

Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelensky said Kyiv had launched rockets, jet and naval drones in a "unique operation" to strike the Russian base, although he did not mention grain terminals being hit.

Ukraine's military later said four Russian warships, including two frigates, were hit. Russia has not commented on the issue.

"The occupying fleet and all the infrastructure that supports it will not be safe as long as Russian aggression continues," Zelensky said in a post on social media.

Most of Russia's Black Sea fleet is docked in Novorossiysk - one of the largest ports in Russia - after it was forced to vacate its former home base of Sevastopol, in the Russia-occupied Crimean peninsula, which was too exposed to Ukrainian attacks.

The attack follows an uptick in the exchange of strikes in the Black Sea this summer, after a period of relative calm.

In an interview with CNN, Zelensky said that Ukraine needs a tenth of the current US stockpile of interceptor missiles to stop all Russian ballistic missile attacks.

He added that 5% of the stockpile would get Ukraine through winter.

"This year we have two and a half times less interceptors than we had in 2025," the Ukrainian president said.

"Russia has two times more ballistic missiles per month than they had before."

A major grain trading company confirmed to Russia's TASS news agency that its terminal had been hit in the attack on Wednesday, while another told Reuters and Russian outlet RBK the same.

The Russian agriculture ministry announced on Wednesday that it was working to redirect cargo flows to ports in the Baltic and Caspian Seas as well as land routes. It did not make any reference to Ukraine's attacks but said it was "taking into account current logistical constraints".

Repeated explosions reportedly rang out over Novorossiysk throughout the night as air defences shot down aerial objects.

An emergency situation was declared in the city on Wednesday, after the barrage of drones struck areas around the port and damaged pipelines, suspending water supply for the city.

Elsewhere in the region a man was killed by drone debris, regional Governor Veniamin Kondratyev said. Several locations in the surrounding Krasnodar region were also struck by "several hundred drones" overnight, Kondratyev added, with dozens of buildings damaged, including homes.

For its part, Moscow launched aerial overnight strikes which killed at least 11 civilians in Ukraine between Tuesday and Wednesday.

The majority were killed when Russia hit the southern city of Zaporizhzhia with ballistic missiles and glide bombs.

News.title: First 100% British chocolate bar made since 1932
News.content:
A chocolate bar has been made using entirely British ingredients for the first time in nearly a century, with cocoa from not Brazil or Bali, but Berkshire.

Created at the University of Reading, it was named the Reading 100 Chocolate Bar to mark the university's 100th anniversary.

It is the first of its kind since 1932, when Rowntree's gifted a six-year-old Princess Elizabeth the only other bar of UK-grown chocolate ever made.

Food security master's student Maha Khan created the chocolate bar by harvesting, fermenting and processing the Reading-grown cocoa.

While the UK's chocolate market is worth Â£10.4bn, it is entirely reliant on imported cocoa.

Maha told the Today programme she made the bar to highlight the challenges facing the cocoa growing industry.

She said: "It is incredible that we can make 100% British chocolate â but in the context of climate change, pests and diseases, there are estimates that 30 to 40% is lost.

"And we've seen with these heatwaves, climate change, these problems and challenges are only going to get exacerbated."

News.title: Results, appeals and resits - what to do if your A-levels don't go to plan
News.content:
Hundreds of thousands of A-level students in England, Wales and Northern Ireland are waiting for their results.

They will be released at 08:00 BST on Thursday 13 August.

Those who have applied to university should be able to see whether they have been successful then too, as the Ucas Hub updates at the same time.

Here is everything you need to know about results, appeals and resits.

News.title: How to get the most out of university clearing on results day
News.content:
Have you changed your mind about the university course you want to start after getting your results?

Maybe you did not apply to university originally but now want to go, or you might not end up getting the grades you need to make it into your firm choice.

If that is you, the clearing process will have you covered.

While students in Scotland received their results last week, young people in England, Wales and Northern Ireland will find out how they did in their exams on Thursday 13 August.

Here is everything you need to know about clearing.

News.title: Students wait for A-level, T-level and BTec results
News.content:
Hundreds of thousands of students in England, Wales and Northern Ireland will receive A-level, T-level and BTec results on Thursday morning.

Another record number of students are expected to find out they have secured a place at their first choice of university.

The cost of going to university has been in the spotlight this year, with mounting pressure on the government to reform student loan repayments, and there has been a renewed focus on technical education under Prime Minister Andy Burnham.

But the chief executive of Universities UK, which represents more than 140 vice-chancellors, urged students to not "let politicians make your decision for you".

About 40% of 18-year-olds in England receive A-levels every summer.

Around 250,000 grades for vocational and technical qualifications are also expected to be released to students in England.

These include BTec National, Cambridge Technical, Cambridge Advanced National and T-level results.

Launched in 2020, T-levels are two-year technical courses that are taken after GCSEs. They focus more on practical subjects than academic ones, but are an equivalent qualification to three A-levels.

AS-levels, which will count towards students' final A-level results next summer in Wales and Northern Ireland, will also be released.

This year, the pass rate for National 5, Higher and Advanced Higher exams in Scotland rose across the board.

And last year, the proportion of students getting top A-level results reached a record high, with 28.3% of all grades across England, Wales and Northern Ireland marked at A* or A.

News.title: I've been fighting wildfires while I wait for my A-level results
News.content:
An 18-year-old firefighter who combined his A-levels with responding to emergency calls is among thousands of students getting results on Thursday morning.

Bobi Jones from Newcastle Emlyn in Carmarthenshire said he felt "quite relaxed" about his grades after having "plenty on my plate" responding to recent wildfires.

As well as A-levels, results for AS, BTec and other vocational qualifications will also be published, with many students hoping to progress to university.

A-level grades can be shared with students from 08:00 BST but arrangements vary depending on the school or college.

Bobi is waiting for results for A-level business and sport, as well as the Welsh Baccalaureate qualification.

He said his school, Ysgol Bro Teifi, had been "very flexible", with teachers allowing him to leave class when his work alarm went off as long as he caught up with schoolwork afterwards.

"The past few months have been very busy with exams and also the fire brigade. We've been really busy with fires and wildfires," he said.

Fortunately the problem has not been as serious as in some areas, but Bobi has been regularly responding to "a few patches of grass going up on fire and just spreading very fast".

He is now planning to take on an apprenticeship with a local electrician which he will combine with on-call shifts for Mid and West Wales Fire and Rescue Service.

Last year, the proportion of A* grades rose slightly to 10.5%, while 29.5% of results were A or A* which was lower than in 2024.

Data shows 32.8% of Welsh 18-year-olds had applied for university places by the end of June - slightly up on last year but lower than figures for other UK nations.

News.title: Burnham urges shops not to sell disposable BBQs over wildfire risks
News.content:
Andy Burnham has urged shops to stop selling disposable barbecues amid increased wildfire risk driven by this summer's droughts.

The prime minister said he was urging "all retailers big and small" to adhere to voluntary guidance to suspend sales during extreme heat.

He added that in the "longer term" the government would look at potentially banning the single-use grills during summer months.

It comes after a potential ban was discussed at an emergency Cobra meeting on the government's response to record temperatures.

A number of large retailers and supermarkets have voluntarily stopped selling the devices under a framework, external agreed in 2023 between fire chiefs and the British Retail Consortium (BRC).

This says that retailers should suspend sales once an extreme heat event has been declared as imminent, or in response to "reasonable, evidence based" requests from local councils.

Earlier, Burnham told reporters single-use grills had been behind a number of recent blazes and people should not be using them "at this moment in time".

"We do want people to take the greatest possible care when they are out in the countryside, both in terms of cigarettes, but also those temporary barbecues that we know are causing risk of fires."

After the Cobra meeting, Burnham said: "We would say to retailers do not put disposable barbecues on sale at this moment in time."

Nearly three-quarters of England and all of Wales have been officially declared in drought, creating conditions rife for fire to spread.

The Met Office has issued a rare amber extreme heat warning for Thursday, with temperatures peaking in the mid-to-high 30s across the Midlands and south-east of England, and a high of 38C possible.

News.title: GB's Hudson-Smith wins historic 400m gold on home track
News.content:
On his childhood track, in front of a stand named in his honour, hometown hero Matthew Hudson-Smith was not going to be denied.

A full-circle moment, completed by writing his name in history.

More than two decades after stepping foot inside Alexander Stadium for the first time aged nine, Hudson-Smith delivered Great Britain's latest gold in Birmingham to become the joint-most decorated man of all-time at European Championships.

The 31-year-old celebrated the third European 400m title of his illustrious career by making his way into the crowd and placing a hand on the banner bearing his name.

Moments before, Hudson-Smith had stormed down the home straight, just as he had countless times before as a member of local club Birchfield Harriers.

This time, though, the Olympic and world silver medallist did so to rapturous cheers inside the arena which fostered his love for the sport.

With his eighth podium at the championships, Hudson-Smith equalled French sprinter Christophe Lemaitre's men's record medal tally - with the relays still to come.

"Honestly, words can't describe how much that meant to me," he told BBC Sport.

"Nobody was going to beat me on this track. This is my home. I know this track like the back of my hand. I have my stand. Now I'm going to go for Mayor of Birmingham and Wolverhampton!

"I knew I was the best in the world. I knew that, on paper, I was a second faster than every single one of these guys. It was about me and the clock."

News.title: Scottish Labour leader hopefuls warn against party divisions
News.content:
Scottish Labour leadership contenders have warned about the dangers of internal feuds and briefings at their first party hustings in Glasgow.

Monica Lennon, Joe Fagan and Michael Marra made their cases to succeed Anas Sarwar as they pitched to rebuild Scottish Labour after May's crushing electoral defeat.

Those attending the hour-long event were met by a handful of pro-Palestine protesters, whose shouts were heard during the first part of the event.

All three candidates promised to change, rebuild and unite the party following its worst Holyrood election defeat since devolution.

News.title: New Forest wildfire continues as temperatures rise
News.content:
Firefighters on the fourth day of battling a wildfire in the New Forest are facing "challenging" weather conditions with temperatures set to rise again

The blaze began on Sunday 9 August when a van caught fire on the A31, with 23 drivers abandoning their vehicles as the fire took hold.

Hampshire & Isle of Wight Fire and Rescue Service (HIWFRS) said crews had implemented fire breaks and had a 'good hold' of the perimeter of the fire, while changing wind conditions were proving challenging.

National Highways said repairs to the A31 were not expected to be begin until Friday 14 August at the earliest.

News.title: Green councillor charged with assaults
News.content:
A Birmingham Green Party city councillor has been charged with attacking a member of the public, three police officers and a member of police staff.

Siobhan Harper-Nunes, 66, was arrested on suspicion of assault after police were called to the junction of Monument Road and Hagley Road in the city, at about 17:00 BST on Thursday.

Harper-Nunes, of Monument Road, was charged on Friday.

West Midlands Police said that she was arrested again at Monument Road on Wednesday morning on suspicion of harassment.

She remained in custody while inquiries continued, police said.

Harper-Nunes will appear at Birmingham Magistrates' Court on 10 September on the assault charges, the force said.

The councillor was elected in May to represent the Ladywood ward for the city council.

She previously stood as the Green Party's candidate for West Midlands mayor in the 2024 election.

The Birmingham Green Party has been approached for comment.

News.title: Victim of fatal Clapham shooting named
News.content:
A man who was shot dead in south-west London has been named by police as Auguste-Marie Bile-aka Amoa.

Officers and paramedics were called to Willington Road, Clapham, just before 22:00 BST on Monday following reports of gunshots near The Landor pub.

The 25-year-old, who worked as a bus driver, was pronounced dead at the scene, the Metropolitan Police said.

A 22-year-old man was later arrested on suspicion of murder after attending hospital with a gunshot wound on Tuesday. He remains in hospital under police guard.

Det Ch Insp Claire Guiver said her thoughts were with the victim's family as they "come to terms with this tragic incident".

News.title: This tranquil hotel in Osaka was so relaxing I didn’t want to leave
News.content:

Located at the heart of Japan’s famous foodie city, Four Seasons Osaka is a stylish city hotel and wellness retreat with amazing views from every angle

Location

Located within the One Dojima skyscraper, in the upscale Dojima district, Four Seasons Osaka offers a quiet sanctuary only minutes from some of the Japanese city's most high-end spots. Kitashinchi, famous for its exclusive nightlife and fine dining, is only a five-minute walk from the hotel, while a five-minute walk over a bridge leads to the scenic and sophisticated Nakanoshima district, a three-kilometre island between the Dōjima and Tosabori rivers.

If arriving by air, from Kansai International airport (KIX) the drive is around 50 minutes while the train is 45 minutes to JR Osaka Station followed by a three-minute taxi ride. From Osaka Itami Airport (ITM), expect a 25-minute drive to the hotel.



The vibe

Set within the 49-storey One Dojima skyscraper, and occupying 12 floors, this urban sanctuary feels residential yet elevated in style. The ground floor sets an intentionally grounded tone with curated art pieces, a light-filled arrival lounge and Jardin, its open and airy French bistro, which is surrounded by greenery.

On the top 10 floors, public lounges and guest accommodation offer panoramic views of the Dojima River, the cityscape and Osaka Castle.

open image in gallery Bathe with a view at Four Seasons Osaka ( Four Seasons )

A fusion of French and Japanese style is woven into many aspects of the hotel, from Jardin to the interior design, which is a collaboration between Tokyo-based Nikken Sekkei and SIMPLICITY, and French-born designer Gwenael Nicolas (of CURIOSITY). The look merges contemporary luxury with traditional elements; milled timber, sliding shoji screens and a dedicated modern ryokan floor with quiet, shoe-free tatami-matted walkways.

The service

The service is impeccable. I found myself enjoying friendly small talk with multiple members of staff on each day of my stay.

From accommodating a takeaway bento box breakfast for an early morning start to suggesting a cocktail that fit my mood at Bar Bota, I felt taken care of throughout the duration of my stay.

Bed and bath

Four Seasons Osaka has 148 guest rooms and 27 suites. The Western-style guest rooms and suites span floors 29 to 35, which are minimalist in design, and feature sliding doors. Oversized bathtubs in full marble bathrooms extend the spa-like experience from the 36th floor wellness facilities into your private space.

open image in gallery Views are impressive from every room ( Four Seasons )

The city skyline is the focal point of each guest room. As you lay in bed at night with the city lit up by the surrounding landscape you’ll feel as though you’re in a movie. If bright lights aren’t for you, the blackout roller shades can turn your room pitch black at the flick of a switch.

On the 28th floor you’ll find the hotel’s modern ryokan-style rooms. There are 21, which feature tatami mat flooring, sliding doors, and low seating. The bathrooms are decorated in stone, with black tiles and dark timber detailing. These rooms are in high demand, and after a night in one of them I understood why. They are designed to foster a feeling of peace and relaxation – exactly what one would want in a hotel room. The communal SABO tea lounge is only steps away and extends the feeling of zen.



Food and drink

Jardin is the hotel’s French bistro where a buffet breakfast is served. Dishes include taiyaki pancakes, an Osaka-style savoury waffle topped with fried chicken and the Farine croissant Benedict, with a poached egg, avocado, seasonal microgreens, shaved parmesan cheese and a lime wedge (it was one of the best pastries I’ve ever had). As the restaurant works closely with the hotel’s artisanal bakery, Farine, next door, fresh pastries and brioche are a core part of the menu.

Unsurprisingly, the other food and drink spots also live up to Osaka’s reputation as the food capital of Japan. Sushi L'Abysse Osaka Yannick Alléno is an omakase counter that combines French haute cuisine techniques with Japanese sushi artistry.

open image in gallery Jardin, the hotel’s Japanese-French fusion bistro and buffet restaurant ( Four Seasons )

Jiang Nan Chun is the hotel’s signature Cantonese fine dining restaurant, located on the 37th floor. The high ceilings and dim lighting add a certain moodiness while you enjoy the menu, crafted by executive Chinese chef, Raymond Wong. Standout dishes include the wok-fried A5 wagyu beef and shishito pepper with barbecue sauce, and braised pumpkin soup with black truffle and elm fungus. Next door is Bar Bota, a cocktail bar with panoramic views of the city skyline.

SABO, the tea and saki lounge, is an exclusive experience for guests staying in the Gensui tatami rooms and suites, and is modelled after a traditional Japanese ryokan tea house.

The Four Seasons is thorough in its accommodation of dietary needs. Menus are clearly labelled with everything from preferences (including vegan or vegetarian) to allergens (such as celery and buckwheat), and there are plenty of dedicated plant-based and vegetarian options.

Facilities

open image in gallery Guests can book private ofuros (Japanese soaking tubs) ( Four Seasons )

The 36th-floor wellness centre is truly something special. The entire floor is a dedicated sanctuary that includes an indoor heated pool with city views from floor-to-ceiling windows, a 24-hour fitness centre, public and private ofuros (Japanese soaking tubs) and five naturally-lit treatment rooms for spa therapies. The pool and ofuros are open for use from 6:30am to 10pm, making them the perfect place to start or end the day.

For events, Four Seasons Osaka also has a grand ballroom and garden terrace, along with an intimate private venue that can be booked for up to 14 guests.



Accessibility

The hotel has four fully accessible rooms, along with a step-free entryway with gentle slopes and automatic doors. There are wheelchair accessible elevators that connect guests from the main lobby to all guest room levels.

Pet policy

No pets are allowed, except certified service animals.

open image in gallery SABO tea lounge is the best place to take Instagram pictures ( Four Seasons )

Check-in/check-out

Check-in is from 3pm, check-out is noon.

Family-friendly?

The hotel offers a kids’ menu along with babysitting services for a fee. However, the crowd leans more adult, with many people staying for business rather than pleasure.

At a glance

Best thing: The ryokan-style rooms, offering an authentic Japanese experience.

Perfect for: Business travellers and those wanting a relaxing city centre base.

Not right for: A family-focused holiday.

Instagram from: SABO tea lounge with views of city skyline out the windows.

Address: 2-4-32 Dojima, Kita-ku, Osaka 530-0003, Japan

Phone:+81 6 6676 8682

Website: fourseasons.com/osaka



Niki was a guest of Four Seasons Osaka
