World.title: Bill proposes banning people convicted of serious crimes from changing their name
World.content:
The Ministry of the Interior has submitted a draft Personal Names Act to the government for approval that would, among other things, restrict the right of people convicted of serious crimes to obtain a new name.

The Personal Names Act will replace the Names Act, which has been in force for more than 20 years. The bill revises terminology, clarifies what name-related procedures entail and overhauls the process for granting a new name at a person's request, the ministry said.

One of the bill's most significant changes would permanently bar people who have committed particularly serious crimes from obtaining a new name by any means.

Interior Minister Igor Taro (Eesti 200) said the changes must meet society's expectations while helping ensure public safety and maintain trust.

"Particularly serious crimes are not committed by accident, and this is an area where we must put everyone's safety first. We cannot allow a situation in which people convicted of terrorism, war crimes, crimes against the state or serious crimes against the person can use a new name to conceal their past or avoid being linked to their previous actions," Taro said.

Under the bill, the restriction would apply to people who have committed crimes including crimes against humanity, genocide, aggression, war crimes, terrorism, crimes against the state, organizing mass disorder and serious offenses involving explosives or explosive materials.

"The seriousness of these crimes and their impact on society are such that it is in the public interest for the identities of their perpetrators to remain clear and traceable," the interior minister stressed.

The existing Names Act's restriction on name changes for people convicted of sexual offenses against minors, which was recently added at the proposal of the Riigikogu, will be carried over. The new Personal Names Act would likewise impose a lifelong restriction on name-related procedures for those convicted of sexual offenses against minors.

The bill also clarifies the rules for granting a new surname at a person's request.

In the future, people choosing a surname freely will not be able to select one already held by a living person listed in the Population Register. The change is intended to prevent the appearance of a family or kinship relationship and reduce the risk of identity theft.

At the same time, the new rules will allow new Estonian-style surnames to be created, helping develop Estonia's naming tradition.

The options for changing a minor's surname will also be narrowed. In the future, a minor may only be given a surname held by one of their parents. The change is intended to protect the child's interests, ensure continuity of identity and maintain a clear connection with their family.

The new law is expected to enter into force in 2028.

World.title: Expert: Presidential election looks set to head to electoral college
World.content:
The political situation being as it is means the presidential election process due to start next month will likely head to the electoral college, politics expert Annika Arras said.

This is despite an apparent desire to get the next head of state voted in at the Riigikogu in early September, Arras told "Aktuaalne kaamera."

Is Ülle Madise now that person the Riigikogu can find consensus on?

One might hope; the reality is different. The numbers indicate it will not be so easy. As the decision has been made, [nomination] signatures [from MPs] will start to get collected on Wednesday, but no one has expressed outright opposition, so there is a chance.

How should we look at Urmas Reinsalu's desire, and that of other politicians, to get acquainted with Ülle Madise and her views? Is Madise an unknown quantity to politicians?

She is likely not entirely unknown to them, and I believe they will all have encountered her in the course of their political careers, both directly and thanks to her public appearances. That said, there is nothing strange about wanting to meet, to hear Ülle Madise's views in more detail, for example on foreign policy and security issues, as well as on domestic matters, family policy and so on. That should certainly go ahead.

It is clear that there is currently some disagreement over the correct timing, but from a citizen's perspective I would certainly like to hear Madise's views as a potential presidential candidate, at the earliest available opportunity.

Annika Arras. Source: Priit Mürk/ERR

How should Tiit Land's candidacy be seen? Has he been put forward to guarantee that the election moves from the Riigikogu to the electoral college, as the opposition would like to happen?

This is always a possibility. During the presidential election process, it should also be borne in mind that we have Riigikogu elections in six months' time, and the opposition's task is to establish a narrative that will help it, heading into those elections. With that in mind, they are not going to immediately rally behind the coalition's candidate, which Ülle Madise is nevertheless now emerging as, even as she herself does not want to be that. She wants to be a candidate for all, and has expressed clearly her desire to remain impartial. Come what may, having alternative candidates serves the opposition's aims. There is right now a willingness to reach consensus at the Riigikogu, but it still seems more likely that the matter will ultimately head to the electoral college.

How likely is it that the electoral college will consider the candidates who have already been put forward? Or is there still a "dark horse" candidate yet to emerge?

An increasing number of candidates have emerged in recent weeks, so nothing should be ruled out. Since the window for nominating candidates is still pretty short, more new names may emerge only once it becomes clear that the Riigikogu is unable to elect a president.

Everyone is saying there needs to be a presidential debate. Could you imagine all these respected people arguing with each other and angrily throwing arguments to and fro? What would a debate like that look like?

If a debate were to take place, it could be a substantive one. ERR has every opportunity to organize a substantive discussion of that kind. When I look at the presidential elections our northern neighbor Finland has, though the electoral system is different, presidential candidates there discuss foreign policy and economic policy, as well as other issues. All the candidates are given equal air time, and the discussion is not adversarial, but substantive. I believe Estonia needs the same thing.

Background:

The presidential candidate nomination window runs Aug. 21-24, with the three Riigikogu ballots to follow Sept. 2-3, with at least 68 votes required. If these draw a blank, the process heads to a 208-member-strong regional electoral college, which convenes in Tallinn. If this, too, fails to get a president elected, the matter returns to the Riigikogu, with parliament's Council of Elders – the speaker, their two deputies, and the heads of the six elected party factions – having the final say on a candidate to be voted on. This last happened in October 2016 when Kersti Kaljulaid was elected president. You can read more about the potential candidates so far, here.

World.title: Andrus Kaarelson: If we do not act fast investments will go to Latvia
World.content:
Estonia's government has failed to attract foreign investment. Companies are choosing our neighbors instead. Now we cannot even distribute major investment support because there are simply no investors, Andrus Kaarelson writes.

Everyone who has been at the helm of the state in recent years should take responsibility. Our NIMBY culture ("not in my backyard") has grown beyond all reason. It is impossible to make any major energy or industrial investment in Estonia without years of disputes with a local municipality or even in court.

You cannot even build a poultry farm. A few years ago, when interest in building the Väimela large poultry farm faded, OÜ Lõuna-Eesti Talumuna leader Tõnu Vetik summed up Estonia's investment climate well: "It is not possible to build anything big in Estonia, whether wind turbines, poultry farms or pulp mills."

Investors are rational and prefer countries that welcome major investments instead of tripping them up at every turn. The state has had years to change this attitude. Officials talk about making planning easier, but real steps have been few and investor trust has not grown.

"The government essentially admitted it has failed to attract major investments."

Problems with actually completing investments have been made worse by the unstable economic environment created after the 2023 elections. Constant and wide-ranging tax changes — always upward — have led foreign investors to look past Estonia. They prefer countries where taxes remain stable between drafting a business plan and completing an investment, so the plan still works.

This leaves Estonians poorer. Fewer competitive jobs mean lower wages and more unemployment. Unfortunately, the governing parties do not seem to understand this.

While neighboring countries are receiving foreign investments worth billions of euros, Estonia is trying to scrape together small investments to save what can be saved.

Recently we learned that the application threshold for support of up to €20 million — previously meant for companies investing at least €100 million in Estonia — was lowered by several tens of millions to €70 million. For defense industry projects it was lowered to €20 million, and for priority technology (which includes food production and renewable energy) to €30 million.

The government essentially admitted it has failed to attract major investments and now must lower the €100 million bar because applicants simply did not come. Under the previous conditions, the roughly €40 million available for support this year cannot be distributed. Major investment support should not be scattered randomly, and the government must start working seriously to find large investments.

"If the trend continues, our southern neighbors will soon pass us."

This comes at a time when Germany's Rheinmetall alone is investing about half a billion euros in Lithuania, Finland is building data centers worth billions, and Poland is building a nuclear plant worth billions. Even Latvia received slightly more than €1 billion in foreign investment in 2025. Estonia's figure was nearly twice as low, between €500 million and €800 million depending on the source.

We should not forget that several Estonian entrepreneurs have made their biggest recent investments in Latvia or other nearby countries. These include Frankenburg's €10 million investment in the Ādaži rocket factory and Fibenol's decision to invest €700 million in a Latvian biorefinery.

Skeleton Technologies also did not choose Estonia. Last year it launched super battery production in Varkaus, Finland, and in late November opened supercapacitor factories in Germany and Poland.

Yes, Estonia still has more foreign investment overall than Latvia and Lithuania, but our lead has shrunk sharply in the past year. If the trend continues, our southern neighbors will soon pass us. To prevent that, Estonia's business environment must again become attractive to foreign investors. That requires breaking the NIMBY culture and ending constant tax hikes. Only then can our economy start growing strongly again.

Parempoolsed do not believe that high taxes and large subsidies will bring foreign investment to Estonia. The government has not created a competitive business environment in the past decade. Estonia lacks affordable electricity, fast internet access is still unresolved, and the state's erratic tax policy and heavy bureaucracy drive foreign investors away. It is high time to start improving Estonia's business environment.

World.title: Senior Iraqi security delegation heads to Saudi Arabia
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — A high-level Iraqi security delegation will travel to Riyadh on Thursday, August 13, 2026, to conduct talks regarding recent cross-border drone strikes targeting petroleum infrastructure in Saudi Arabia, according to a senior government source.

The delegation will be led by General Abdul-Amir Al-Shammari, Director of the Office of the Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces, alongside Iraqi National Intelligence Service (INIS) Chief Hamid Al-Shatri. The trip follows a reciprocal visit to Baghdad days earlier by Saudi Intelligence Chief Khalid bin Ali Al-Humaidan.

Key Security & Diplomatic Developments

High-Level Delegation: Led by General Abdul-Amir Al-Shammari and Intelligence Chief Hamid Al-Shatri to establish joint intelligence-sharing protocols with Riyadh.

Incident Background: Late last month, the Saudi Ministry of Defense reported intercepting several drones originating from Iraqi territory targeting oil facilities in the Eastern Province and Riyadh.

Domestic Investigation: Prime Minister and Commander-in-Chief Ali Falih al-Zaidi ordered a formal military investigation into the launch origins following the Saudi allegations.

Diplomatic Mediation: The visit comes after international and regional mediation restored diplomatic channels following the cancellation of Prime Minister Al-Zaidi’s planned trip to Riyadh late last month amid joint U.S.-Saudi strikes inside Iraq.

Regional Position: During a recent bilateral meeting in Amman between Saudi Foreign Minister Faisal bin Farhan and Iraqi Foreign Minister Fuad Hussein, Riyadh reaffirmed support for Iraq while stressing the necessity that Iraqi territory not be utilized as a platform for aggression against neighboring states.

The bilateral security summit aims to reinforce radar tracking, anti-drone intelligence sharing, and border surveillance between Baghdad and Riyadh.

While the “Islamic Resistance in Iraq” denied responsibility for the Saudi oil facility strikes, Prime Minister Al-Zaidi’s administration is taking direct steps to prevent unauthorized non-state launches, safeguard Iraqi sovereignty, and protect diplomatic and economic ties with Riyadh.

World.title: Supreme Judicial Council President Faiq Zidan to visit Syria
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — President of the Iraqi Supreme Judicial Council, Judge Faiq Zidan, is scheduled to conduct an official visit to Syria on Thursday, August 13, 2026, marking a landmark first-of-its-kind judicial mission to Damascus, according to a senior official source.

The high-level visit aims to hold structured talks with Syrian judicial authorities to address shared legal frameworks, cross-border judicial coordination, counter-terrorism extradition agreements, and legal mechanisms regulating bilateral trade corridors.

World.title: Iraq Transport Ministry reports 95% completion of Development Road designs
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Minister of Transport Wahab Al-Hasani met with the Parliamentary Transport and Communications Committee on Tuesday, August 11, 2026, to review execution milestones across strategic infrastructure projects, including the Development Road, the Grand Fao Port, and national rail modernization.

During the executive session, Al-Hasani presented technical updates on the 1,200-kilometer Development Road Project, confirming that primary design phases are near completion, with railway engineering blueprints reaching 95% and highway transit designs at 85%.

Key Operational Metrics & Project Milestones

Development Road Project: Designs for the 1,200 km transit corridor are nearly complete (95% for railway tracks, 85% for highways). The MOU executed with Turkey serves as a preliminary framework with no current financial or legal obligations.

Grand Fao Port: Submerged tunnel construction reached 86% completion, alongside advanced structural work across five main container berths.

Rail Network Modernization: Ministry teams are actively pursuing the rehabilitation of the Baghdad–Mosul–Rabia railway corridor extending toward the Syrian border.

Maritime Fleet Mobilization: State maritime companies confirmed readiness to deploy Iraqi vessels to transport crude oil and refined petroleum products to support alternative national export strategies.

Administrative & Executive Actions: Al-Hasani confirmed the suspension of Iraqi Airways’ former Director-General and two deputies following an internal investigative audit.

Legislative Alignment: Agreement reached to draft amendments to Transport Law No. 80 of 1983 and establish a joint parliamentary-executive committee holding weekly meetings to update transport regulations.

The meeting highlights Iraq’s strategy to transform into a central logistics bridge connecting the Gulf to Europe, bypassing maritime transit chokepoints.

By pairing the Grand Fao Port’s advancing infrastructure with overland rail links extending north to Turkey and west through the Baghdad–Mosul–Rabia line toward Syria, the Ministry of Transport is laying the groundwork for integrated commercial supply chains across Eurasia.

World.title: MP Abdul Jabbar proposes 145 km pipeline to boost Basra crude to Ceyhan
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Independent MP and Secretary-General of the Fao–Zakho Coalition, Amer Abdul-Jabbar, proposed a plan on Wednesday, August 12, 2026, to construct a 145-kilometer oil pipeline link to transport Basra crude north toward Turkey’s Ceyhan terminal.

Abdul-Jabbar stated via social media that the proposed missing link would instantly increase Iraq’s northern export capacity by 150,000 to 300,000 barrels per day (bpd). To avoid drawing on the federal budget during the ongoing liquidity crisis, he advocated launching a “National Volunteer Effort,” utilizing surplus piping from state-owned enterprises alongside logistical backing from private contractors operating under Ministry of Oil contracts.

Key Technical & Strategy Highlights

Proposed Pipeline Link: A 145 km strategic bypass connecting southern oilfields in Basra directly to northern export routes toward the Turkish port of Ceyhan.

Capacity Increase: Designed to boost crude export flows by 150,000 to 300,000 bpd, mitigating bottlenecks caused by Persian Gulf shipping disruptions.

Zero-Cost Volunteer Framework: Proposed execution via a “National Volunteer Effort” using inventory audits of unused piping across state firms and private sector contractor support.

Existing Ministry Export Strategy: Complements Oil Minister Basim Mohammed Khudair’s August 9 plan to export 750,000 bpd to Ceyhan via: 450,000 bpd pumped through the Strategic Pipeline after rehabilitating the PS3 pump station in Najaf and K3 in Haditha. 300,000 bpd transported via road tankers (including 200,000 bpd through KAR Group and 100,000 bpd under a secondary contract).

Long-Term Iraqi-Turkish Energy Framework: Ministry of Oil is finalizing a 1-year interim agreement with Ankara, paving the way for a 10- to 20-year strategic partnership involving Turkish BOTAŞ and BP in developing Kirkuk oilfields.

Abdul-Jabbar’s proposal comes as the Ministry of Oil accelerates alternative land-based export channels to bypass the blocked Strait of Hormuz.

Minister Khudair previously confirmed that Iraq’s State Company for Oil Projects (SCOP) and Turkey’s BOTAŞ are actively inspecting and rehabilitating the northern export system to handle between 500,000 and 750,000 bpd. Implementing the 145 km bypass link could offer Baghdad an immediate, low-cost mechanism to restore crude cash flows while long-term pipeline infrastructure is constructed toward Syria and Jordan.

World.title: Meta meets its own ‘tobacco’ moment in court
World.content:
Oakland – With billions of users around the world, Meta will defend itself against allegations of harming children in a new trial in the United States this week, which experts describe as social media’s big tobacco moment.

After a coalition of states sued Meta in 2023 for allegedly designing addictive features for kids in its apps, four states were selected to represent their claims: California, Colorado, Kentucky and New Jersey.

Top prosecutors of those states now aim to prove in federal court that Meta deliberately made Facebook and Instagram addictive for children.

Meta “strongly disagrees with these allegations” and is “confident the evidence will show our longstanding commitment to supporting young people,” a spokesperson told AFP, adding that the company has “listened to parents, worked with experts and law enforcement.”

Although it’s not the first lawsuit that seeks to hold a social media company accountable for its impact on mental health and safety, it could become one of the most consequential.

“It really feels like tobacco in the 1990s,” Vincent Joralemon, a director at Berkeley’s Life Sciences Law and Policy Center, told AFP.

While these cases about social media harms revolve around the intersection of technology and addiction, the legal argument in this case against Meta centers on its business practices, just like when the federal government sued tobacco companies around three decades ago, Joralemon said.

By the early 1990s, decades of research showed that tobacco use caused health problems such as cancer, and eventually additional investigations revealed how the industry deliberately downplayed, and even concealed, the harmful impacts of its products.

– ‘Protecting teens’ –

Dozens of US states sued four major tobacco companies, and by 1998, won a landmark settlement agreement which included financial penalties and changes to how products were marketed, particularly to children whom the industry targeted with s featuring cartoon characters, the most famous of which was known as “Joe Camel.”

Jury selection begins today in Oakland, a short drive from San Francisco and opening statements are expected to begin August 18.

Meta was convicted on similar grounds in separate trials held in Los Angeles and New Mexico, with combined damages that approach $1 billion.

In Oakland, the states are demanding a long list of changes to Meta’s apps, in addition to financial penalties as high as $1.4 trillion, close to Meta’s entire market value which hovers around $1.5 trillion.

Despite the eye-popping number, money isn’t Meta’s biggest problem, if it were to lose the case.

“The huge issue here is reputational harm” and being forced to make major changes, Joralemon said.

“Putting a CEO on the witness stand can be quite damning,” as well, he said.

Meta founder and chief Mark Zuckerberg is among the star witnesses expected to testify.

The case could be “the beginning of a broader reckoning” for Meta, Nora Freeman Engstrom told AFP via email. She is a law professor and associate dean at Stanford.

It will be important to see the “gap” between what Meta knew privately and what it disclosed publicly, Engstrom said.

Meta is “confident in our record of protecting teens online and will continue to defend ourselves against claims that misrepresent the facts,” Meta told AFP last week.

With so many plaintiffs suing Meta and other social media companies, these lawsuits could potentially “go on for decades,” Joralemon said.

In May, Snap, TikTok, YouTube and Meta settled with a school district in Kentucky for $27 million to avoid another trial that was expected to set a precedent for around 1,200 similar lawsuits.

On Monday, a federal appeals court ruled that more than 3,000 additional lawsuits filed against Meta, YouTube-parent Google, Snap and TikTok can proceed.

World.title: Colombia rescuers find woman alive as quake death toll passes 240
World.content:
Pereira – Colombian rescuers pulled a 32-year-old woman alive from the rubble of a collapsed building Tuesday, sparking cheers and applause as exhausted crews raced to find more survivors from the country’s strongest earthquake in a century.

Daniela Largo was carried from the wreckage wrapped in a blue blanket as rescuers embraced and relatives shouted out with joy.

The rescue came as soldiers, firefighters and volunteers searched collapsed buildings across western Colombia after a 7.4-magnitude quake killed at least 241 people and injured more than 1,600.

“We were losing hope and then we received a call,” said her mother Sandra Milena Perez in Pereira.

Perez said a local resident heard cries for help beneath the rubble and joined neighbors in removing debris before professional rescuers arrived.

“Thanks to him, today we’re happy,” she said. “At home her 12-year-old son is waiting for her.”

In Pereira and in Cali, emergency crews used cranes, dogs and heavy machinery to search ruined buildings while volunteers formed human chains to clear debris by hand, hoping to reach people still trapped beneath collapsed structures.

As darkness fell, families prepared to sleep in parks as aftershocks rattled damaged neighborhoods where entire blocks had been reduced to rubble.

The quake overwhelmed parts of the health system, turning the rescue effort into one of Colombia’s largest disaster responses in years.

“The house came down on top of us. I wasn’t able to get out,” said Beatriz Arcos, who was trapped with her husband and mother beneath their collapsed condominium.

“It took about an hour to get us out.” Arcos said she was hospitalized after a concrete block fell on her back. Her husband and mother were also injured.

In Cali, residents armed with picks, shovels and their bare hands joined firefighters in digging through collapsed buildings.

Rescuers stopped every few minutes to call into the rubble and listen for any response.

“We’re doing this with our hands, with gloves” said volunteer Pablo Cesar Ruiz “It’s sad to see time slipping away.”

In Pereira, army units and sniffer dogs combed through twisted concrete and exposed steel.

At one site, a rescue squad leader abruptly raised his fist, stopping workers so they could listen for signs of life.

Volunteers formed human chains, passing bricks and chunks of masonry hand-to-hand to clear paths into collapsed structures.

– ‘So much effort’ –

For many families, the desperate search was becoming a vigil.

“My aunt lived there. She’s under the rubble,” said Jorge Gonzalez, standing beside a collapsed building in Pereira.

“I arrived yesterday and I haven’t left, and until they find her body I don’t intend to leave here.”

While some families waited for news of missing relatives, others were grappling with the loss of homes, possessions and livelihoods.

“We lost everything,” said Stella Galvis, fighting back tears after escaping the collapse of her home.

“We survived by a miracle, since I managed to get my little boy out and my partner managed to get out too.”

From the air, neighborhoods in Cali appeared flattened, with piles of grey rubble replacing entire blocks of homes and apartment buildings.

Nearby, cars lay crushed beneath fallen walls and concrete slabs.

On one mound of debris, a young couple climbed over broken masonry searching for belongings.

They recovered a box from inside a child’s bright red bedside table.

Many survivors spent the night outdoors, either because their homes were damaged or because they feared aftershocks.

One park in Pereira was transformed into a makeshift shelter with tents and mattresses.

“We lost everything, but we’re alive,” said 23-year-old John Tabasco, who was camped there with his wife and seven-month-old son.

“We’ve never had to do this before, to depend on someone else to help us. It’s amazing how life can change.”

Others struggled to come to terms with losing homes built over decades.

“You buy a little house with so much effort, spending 40, 50 years struggling to get yourself that house, you finally get it and in just a few days it all goes down the drain,” said 79-year-old Jaime Alzate.

In Cali, part of the Hospital Universitario del Valle collapsed during the quake, forcing doctors to move patients into a parking lot and treat some in the open air.

Yet amid the destruction, many Colombians mobilized to help.

Thousands brought water, food and supplies to affected neighborhoods, while long lines formed outside blood donation centers.

“It’s about wanting to help your community, your city and your country,” said blood donor Ferney Cabrera.

President Abelardo de la Espriella declared a state of emergency and promised rent subsidies for affected families Tuesday during a visit to Pereira.

The United States announced $15.5 million in emergency aid, while messages of support and offers of assistance arrived from around the world.

As aftershocks continued to rattle damaged cities, rescue crews pressed on through the ruins, hoping more voices, taps or whistles might still emerge.

World.title: Passengers rescued as second ferry in days catches fire in Indonesia
World.content:
Mataram – A navy vessel and other ships rushed in Wednesday to rescue over 100 people from a ferry on fire off the tourist island of Bali, officials said, in the second such incident in days.

There were no immediate reports of casualties among the passengers and crew, with at least 114 people on board, according to the manifest.

The passenger ferry had been sailing from Bali to the next-door island of Lombok when it caught fire in the early morning hours.

Muhamad Hariyadi, head of the search and rescue agency at Mataram on Lombok island, said the total number of passengers on board was being verified.

He said passengers were evacuated on at least three different vessels, including a navy ship and another ferry.

Search and rescue vessels were at the scene and a helicopter was conducting surveillance from the air.

“As of now, we have not received any report of casualties,” Hariyadi told Metro TV.

“We have approached the ship and confirmed that all passengers are no longer on board,” he added. “We visually see no passengers on the ship.”

Last week, five people died when a ferry caught fire off Java island.

Marine accidents are a regular occurrence in Indonesia — an archipelago of more than 17,000 islands that rely heavily on boat connections.

Lax safety standards and unpredictable weather are the main reasons for the disasters.

A ferry transporting more than 70 people sank while sailing near Selayar, a small island south of Sulawesi, last month.

Four bodies were recovered, but the search operation ended with 14 others still officially missing.

World.title: Charges dropped against Bondi Beach attack hero
World.content:
Sydney – Australian police dropped assault charges on Wednesday against a man lauded for his bravery during last year’s mass shooting at Bondi Beach.

Fruit seller Ahmed al Ahmed was hailed as a hero after footage showed him disarming a gunman during the December 14 attack, which killed 15 people at a Jewish festival.

Ahmed was earlier this year accused of stalking and assaulting his father, charges he denied.

Both charges were withdrawn after a brief hearing on Wednesday, court documents showed.

Ahmed ducked between parked cars as the Bondi shooting unfolded, grabbing one of the two gunmen and wresting away his weapon in an effort to stop the killing.

He sustained gunshot wounds in the attack.

Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese would later meet Ahmed in person, describing him as a “true Australian hero” and an inspiration to all.

World.title: Govt notifies Rs 3,030-crore scheme for three mega chemical parks
World.content:
The Bharat Audyogik Vikas Yojana Rasayan (BHAVYA Rasayan) scheme, announced in the Union Budget for 2026-27, was cleared by the Cabinet chaired by PM Modi.

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The Centre has formally notified the BHAVYA Rasayan scheme to establish three greenfield chemical parks across the country, paving the way for states to compete for projects aimed at boosting domestic chemical manufacturing, reducing import dependence and attracting investment.The Gazette notification issued by the Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilisers operationalises the scheme approved by the Union Cabinet last month. With a total outlay of Rs 3,030 crore, the scheme will run from 2026-27 to 2030-31 and support the creation of shared industrial infrastructure for the chemical sector.Under the scheme, the Centre will provide up to Rs 1,000 crore for each chemical park, subject to the concerned state contributing at least Rs 500 crore. Any expenditure beyond this will have to be borne by the state government. Each park must have a minimum 8 sq km (2,000 acres) of contiguous, encumbrance-free land.The parks will be selected through a challenge-based competitive process, with proposals evaluated on predefined quantitative and qualitative parameters, including strategic relevance, financial viability, implementation plans and long-term sustainability.According to the notification, the parks will provide common facilities such as central effluent treatment plants, hazardous waste management systems, water supply, solvent recovery and distillation units, steam generation and distribution networks, interconnected pipelines, logistics infrastructure, laboratory testing centres and emergency response facilities, enabling industries to reduce costs and improve environmental compliance.The government said the scheme is aimed at strengthening the entire chemical value chain, enhancing domestic production capacity, improving cost competitiveness, promoting exports and import substitution, attracting domestic and foreign investment, and generating employment, while contributing to the goal of Viksit Bharat 2047.

World.title: From New York to Delaware: US states to commemorate 'India Day' on August 15
World.content:
Delaware has proclaimed August 15, 2026, as âIndia Dayâ, joining New York and New Jersey in recognising India's Independence Day and the contributions of the Indian-American community ahead of the country's 80th Independence Day.

The proclamation was issued by Delaware Governor Matthew Meyer, who highlighted the state's growing Indian-American community and its contributions to the state's social and economic life.

The development was shared by the Consulate General of India in New York on August 13.

According to the proclamation, Delaware is strengthened by the many cultures and traditions represented across its communities, including its Indian-American population.

Delaware honours Indian-American community

The proclamation said Delawareans of Indian heritage have enriched the state through their work, leadership and service, contributing to shared prosperity and creating opportunities for future generations.

It also highlighted India's diversity of languages, traditions, faiths and customs, noting that generations of Indian Americans have carried these traditions forward while building communities in the US.





The proclamation said India Day would provide an opportunity to honour India's independence, celebrate the heritage and achievements of Delaware's Indian-American community and recognise the enduring connections between Delaware and the people of India.

Governor Meyer encouraged residents to participate in the observance and recognise the contributions of the state's Indian-American community.

New York, New Jersey also recognise August 15

Delaware's proclamation follows similar declarations by New York and New Jersey, which recognised August 15, as India's Independence Day.

New Jersey governor Mikie Sherrill issued a proclamation recognising Indian Independence Day across the state. According to the Consulate General of India in New York, the proclamation highlighted the Indian-American community's contributions to New Jersey in areas including education, healthcare, research, technology, business, public service and community leadership.

New York Governor Kathy Hochul also proclaimed August 15 as India Independence Day across the state.

The Consulate said New York's proclamation recognised the Indian-American community's contribution to the state's cultural, economic and civic life, while also highlighting the enduring ties between India and the US.

The Consulate thanked Hochul for the recognition, saying the proclamation celebrated India's journey of independence and the democratic values shared by the two countries.

How US communities celebrate India's Independence Day

India's Independence Day is marked across the US each year through flag-hoisting ceremonies, parades, cultural programmes and community events.

Indian diplomatic missions, including the Embassy of India in Washington and Indian consulates, hold special programmes on August 15. The Indian mission to the United Nations also participates in commemorative events.

Indian-American communities across states organise cultural performances and public celebrations, with local political leaders often participating and highlighting the community's contributions to American society.

Prominent landmarks have also joined the celebrations in previous years, including the Empire State Building in New York and the Space Needle in Seattle, which have been illuminated in the colours of the Indian tricolour for Independence Day events.

India marks 80th Independence Day with focus on youth

The proclamations come as India prepares to celebrate its 80th Independence Day on August 15, 2026.

This year's celebrations will also focus on the commemoration of 150 years of âVande Mataramâ, while placing particular emphasis on âYuva Shaktiâ or youth power.

The celebrations are expected to combine the historical significance of India's freedom movement with recognition of the achievements and contributions of its younger generation.

The growing number of US states formally recognising India's Independence Day also underlines the visibility of the Indian-American community and the broader social, economic and cultural ties between India and the United States.

World.title: Al-Qaida offshoot AQIS behind Red Fort blast in 2025: UNSC report confirms
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The United Nations Security Council (UNSC) has officially attributed the November 2025 blast near Delhiâs iconic Red Fort to Al-Qaida in the Indian Subcontinent (AQIS), according to the 38th report of its Analytical Support and Sanctions Monitoring Team.

The attack on November 10 last year claimed 11 lives.

"Al-Qaida in the Indian Subcontinent (AQIS, not listed) continued to evolve from a fragmented group into a regional terrorist entity; it established logistics and financial networks, working in decentralised, small, scattered cells instead of large units. The attack in November 2025 on the Red Fort in Delhi was officially attributed to AQIS," the report, published on August 10, stated.

The assessment marks a significant shift in the attribution of the Red Fort attack, which had earlier been linked to the Pakistan-based Jaish-e-Mohammed (JeM).

The report noted that one member state had attributed a series of attacks to JeM and also linked the group to the Red Fort blast.

The explosion occurred around 7 pm when a moving Hyundai i20 erupted in flames near the iconic monument.

Investigators identified Umar-e-Nabi as the driver of the car and suspect him of carrying out the attack as a suicide bomber.





Launched in 2014, AQIS is a regional affiliate of Al-Qaida.

The group was formed to expand the organisationâs activities across South Asia, including India, Pakistan, Bangladesh and parts of Afghanistan.

Meanwhile, the latest UNSC assessment also flagged broader concerns over the activities and capabilities of Al-Qaida and Islamic State (ISIL/Daâesh) affiliates.

World.title: Supreme Court pushes 19 states, union territories to notify cancer
World.content:
Supreme Court has stepped up efforts to bring greater uniformity to cancer reporting

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: With the National Cancer Registry Programme covering only a fraction of Indiaâs population and rural cancer surveillance remaining particularly limited, the Supreme Court has stepped up efforts to bring greater uniformity to cancer reporting. The court on Tuesday asked the 19 States and Union Territories that have not yet notified cancer as a notifiable disease to consider doing so, a move that could make reporting of newly detected cases to public health authorities mandatory.Such notification could help plug gaps in cancer surveillance by giving health authorities a more complete picture of the countryâs cancer burden, including where cases are rising and which populations are most affected. The data could in turn help shape policies on prevention, early detection, treatment capacity and allocation of healthcare resources.A bench headed by Chief Justice Surya Kant passed the order on a plea filed by a retired AIIMS doctor after his lawyer Gaurav Bansal told the court that NCRP covers only 10% of population and rural coverage is less than 1%.The push assumes greater significance against the backdrop of the WHOâs latest Global Status Report on Cancer, which estimates that 92% of people globally will be affected by cancer either directly or through a close family member.The report also projects annual cancer cases to rise to nearly 35 million by 2050.The Supreme Court was informed that 17 of Indiaâs 36 States and UTs have already notified cancer, following recommendations of the Parliamentary Standing Committee on Health and Family Welfare. The remaining 19 have now been asked to consider similar action.Dr Pragya Shukla, Head of Clinical Oncology at Delhi State Cancer Institute, said standardised, disease-specific and timely data was essential to track India's changing cancer burden, identify regional and demographic trends, and assess the impact of prevention and treatment programmes. Such a system, she said, would complement existing cancer registries, help identify high-burden areas, improve planning for treatment infrastructure and medicines, and strengthen evidence-based cancer control. Govil added that reliable data would be critical for planning prevention, early detection and resource allocation.The Indian Cancer Society welcomed the intervention, saying national notification could help build a comprehensive cancer surveillance system. âThe Supreme Courtâs intervention is a significant development, and we welcome its direction to the remaining States and Union Territories to move towards cancer notification,â said Jyotsna Govil, Chairperson, Indian Cancer Society, Delhi. However, she stressed that notification alone would not suffice and called for a uniform national framework with common definitions, reporting standards and data protocols to ensure comparable and interoperable data across states.

World.title: FSSAI puts influencers, celebrities on notice over food promotions
World.content:
NEW DELHI: From "boosts immunity" to "rich in nutrients", food claims endorsed by celebrities and social media influencers are now under the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India's (FSSAI) scanner.

In a significant move aimed at curbing misleading promotions, the regulator has warned influencers and celebrities that endorsing unverified food claims could invite legal action, even as it cracked down on manufacturers selling unsafe food products.

The advisory comes at a time when food brands are increasingly relying on digital creators and celebrities to market health drinks, protein supplements, snacks and packaged foods to millions of consumers online.

FSSAI has asked influencers to verify that every claim made by a brand is truthful, scientifically substantiated and compliant with food safety regulations before lending their name or credibility.

The regulator said endorsements are more than s because consumers often trust the people promoting them. It cautioned influencers against amplifying claims such as "boosts immunity" or "rich in nutrients" unless they are backed by evidence and permitted under food laws.





Misleading food s and endorsements, it said, can attract action under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006, and the Food Safety and Standards (Advertising and Claims) Regulations, 2018.

Alongside the advisory, FSSAI prohibited the manufacture, sale and distribution of food products made by M/s Shree Shyam Foods, M/s Bharat Food Products and M/s KDP Food Industry after government laboratories found their ghee and mustard oil products unsafe for consumption.

The regulator also penalised Dharwad Mishra Pedha and Food Processing Industry in Karnataka after its Motichoor laddoos were found to contain Tartrazine at 2,670.5 mg/kg, more than 26 times the permissible limit of 100 mg/kg. Shree Chemfood Pvt Ltd of Gujarat was similarly penalised after samples of iodised salt were found to be substandard and misbranded.

FSSAI has also urged consumers to report misleading food s and celebrity endorsements through its Food Safety Connect platform.

World.title: Use medical tourists' money to treat poor Indians: Panel
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Revenue earned from foreign patients and affluent Indians should help fund treatment for poorer patients, a Parliamentary Standing Committee on Health and Family Welfare has recommended, proposing that corporate hospitals adopt a cross-subsidisation model to make advanced healthcare more affordable.

The panel said hospitals that benefit from government concessions such as subsidised land, tax incentives and 100% foreign direct investment (FDI) should earmark part of the revenue generated from medical tourism and high-paying patients to provide advanced tertiary care to economically weaker Indians.

The recommendation is part of the committee's report on the affordability and accessibility of healthcare, which noted that India's corporate hospital sector has recorded strong growth driven by high-value procedures, rising medical tourism and increasing revenue per occupied bed.

While acknowledging India's emergence as a global healthcare destination, the panel said the benefits of this growth must also reach patients who cannot afford expensive treatment.

Observing that private health insurance penetration in India remains low and out-of-pocket expenditure continues to push many families into financial distress, the committee said a structured cross-subsidy mechanism could improve access to life-saving tertiary care for poorer patients.





It said hospitals receiving government support should share part of the gains from medical tourism and premium-paying patients with economically weaker sections.

The panel also recommended that corporate hospitals reserve a defined quota of beds under government-funded health insurance schemes such as Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY at standard package rates to ensure that beneficiaries have access to advanced treatment at leading private hospitals.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

To address the uneven distribution of healthcare infrastructure, the committee proposed linking government incentives, including subsidised land, tax benefits and FDI facilitation, to investment in tier-2, tier-3 and rural areas. It also recommended expanding public-private partnerships and extending financial and technology support to smaller hospitals in underserved regions.

The recommendations form part of a broader roadmap to make healthcare more affordable. The committee has also proposed capping private hospital room rents in major metropolitan cities at the average tariff of nearby three-star hotels, standardising treatment package rates, improving price transparency and expanding government health spending to reduce out-of-pocket expenditure.

World.title: NEET-PG aspirants get wrong exam city texts after NBEMS glitch
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Hundreds of NEET-PG 2026 aspirants were left confused after receiving incorrect SMS alerts about their allotted examination cities, prompting the National Board of Examinations in Medical Sciences (NBEMS) to issue a clarification that a technical glitch had led to wrong messages being sent to some candidates.

Several candidates reported receiving two different SMSes within hours, each mentioning a different test city. In one such case, an aspirant was first allotted Gudur (Andhra Pradesh) and later received another message assigning Noida (Uttar Pradesh) as the examination city.

In a public notice issued on Wednesday, NBEMS said the test city allocation had been completed as scheduled and uploaded on the official applicant portal.

However, "due to some technical issues", the test city conveyed to some candidates through SMS was incorrect. It said fresh SMSes and emails carrying the correct test city had subsequently been sent to the affected candidates.

The Board advised candidates not to rely on SMS messages and instead verify their allotted examination city through the NBEMS applicant portal, which it said contains the correct details for all candidates.

It also urged aspirants to rely only on official communications and beware of fake websites and misinformation.

The clarification comes just days before the conduct of the national postgraduate medical entrance examination, with candidates already making travel and accommodation arrangements based on their allotted test cities. The confusion triggered anxiety among aspirants, many of whom took to social media to seek clarification after receiving conflicting messages.

NBEMS maintained that the applicant portal carries the correct examination city details and asked candidates to refer to it for authentic information. It said corrected SMSes and emails have been issued wherever required.

World.title: 20 years and waiting: A decade on, SC to hear athlete’s promotion plea junked by HC in 2016
World.content:
NEW DELHI: A national-level sportswoman, employed as a safaiwala (group D employee) in railways since 2003, has been awaiting promotion to group C level for last two decades despite the railway ministryâs policy to grant out-of-turn first promotion to medal-winning employees, a criterion she had fulfilled by winning two medals in national events.

A decade after winning medals but not getting promotion as per the policy, Rajni Rani moved Punjab and Haryana HC in 2016 with a writ petition, which got dismissed on technical grounds. Her appeal against the HC order has been pending in SC since Nov 2016.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

It was last heard on Jan 9, 2017, when a bench of Justices J Chelameswar and A M Sapre admitted her petition and asked the Union govt to file a response in eight weeks. On May 15, 2018, registrar Kapil Mehta had recorded that statement of case had not been filed by any of the parties despite expiry of the time granted.

He had asked for the case to be listed before the court as per rules. However, her petition continued to gather dust till her counsel Wednesday requested a bench headed by CJI Surya Kant for an early hearing.

A visibly unhappy CJI directed the registry to list the petition for hearing on Aug 21.

Rajni said she was due for promotion in 2005 after winning medals but was denied the benefit of first promotion on the ground that one of the four events she had participated in did not qualify as a national event. She said the rules prescribed participation in only two events. Rajni said she had won a bronze medal at 52nd Northern Railway Athletic Meet in Feb 2005, gold medal at 44th Senior National Inter-State competition in July 2004 and represented railways in open National in Mumbai in Sept 2004, securing fourth position.

Rajni was denied a promotion in 2013 despite a directive by Central Administrative Tribunal to railways in Sept 2012 to consider her case. When she challenged the decision, both CAT and HC dismissed her petitions.

World.title: Parliament Monsoon Session Day 19 LIVE: Lok Sabha adjourned sine die; PM Modi, Amit Shah present
World.content:
The Lok Sabha was adjourned sine die on Thursday (August 13, 2026) shortly after the national song ‘Vande Mataram’ was played at the beginning of the last day of the Monsoon Session of Parliament. Both Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Home Minister Amit Shah were present when the national song was played in the House. Scheduled to end today, the Monsoon Session has seen little business (with no Question Hour and several Bills being passed amid disruptions) as the Opposition demanded that Union Home Minister Amit Shah respond to use of police action against NEET-related student protests in New Delhi.

Also read | 31-member parliamentary panel to review FCRA Bill

Mr. Shah on Wednesday (August 12, 2026) said he was willing to have a full debate on the protests against the NEET paper leak, while Parliamentary Affairs Minister Kiren Rijiju stated that the government was ready to “increase the time” allotted for a debate on the issue. Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi, however, rejected the offer of a discussion, stating that the youth wanted answers on who ordered the firing on and police assault of protestors and “not a lecture” from Mr. Shah.

Amid vocal protests by Opposition members, the Lok Sabha passed a Bill on Wednesday (August 12, 2026) to amend the Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) Amendment Act without a debate. The Rajya Sabha on Wednesday (August 12, 2026) passed two more Bills — The National Co-operative Development Corporation (Amendment) Bill, 2026, and the Kerala (Alteration of Name) Bill, 2026. The Upper House has so far passed about 10 Bills, other than some of the Money Bills which were returned to the Lok Sabha, during the stormy Monsoon Session.

World.title: How Tamil Nadu invested in sustained awareness and building trust to shape its organ donation programme
World.content:
From seven deceased donor organ donations in its first year, to 266 in a single year, Tamil Nadu has come a long way in 17 years. Behind the rise is a gradual shift in public perception, shaped by sustained awareness efforts, measures to build confidence, and trust and improvements in the State’s transplant infrastructure and systems.

The numbers tell a compelling story of how far the State has come with regard to organ donation and transplantation. Since 2008, the highest number of deceased organ donors was recorded in 2024, when Tamil Nadu had 268 donors. In 2025, there were 266 donors - 211 men and 55 women. A total of 1,476 organs were utilised - 856 major organs and 620 minor organs and tissues that year, according to the Transplant Authority of Tamil Nadu’s data.

On World Organ Donation Day, which falls on August 13, experts revisit the milestones, the lessons learnt and the road ahead.

How it worked

J. Amalorpavanathan, founder-member secretary, Transplant Authority of Tamil Nadu, said, “When we started in 2008, the concept of brain death was scarcely understood among healthcare professionals. A few coordinated brain death certifications were happening sporadically, with MOHAN Foundation [an NGO] coordinating around two to three such cases a year in a few city hospitals. The State government had decided to start the Cadaver Transplant Programme (CTP), and the groundwork began in April. We went on to issue 10 government orders. It was in September that year that the parents of 15-year-old Hithendran (who had sustained severe injuries in a road accident and was declared brain dead) decided to donate his organs. The CTP was launched in October 2008, and Hithendran’s case helped organ donation pick up in the State.”

Recalling his visits to all districts, he said that initially, there was reluctance among doctors. “But whenever I interacted with the general public, I found a sense of receptiveness. In fact, though they had questions and sought clarifications, I found the least resistance among them. We slowly convinced healthcare professionals to certify brain death. We had seven donations in the first year, and crossed 180 in a year in eight years. Though the number of organ donations dipped during the COVID-19 pandemic, it picked up again thereafter,” he pointed out.

Families coming forward

Sunil Shroff, managing trustee of MOHAN Foundation, said there had been a tremendous improvement in awareness levels over the years. “Earlier, we found it hard to obtain consent for organ donation. Now, many families are coming forward to donate. In States such as Tamil Nadu and Telangana, where awareness is relatively high, I think that 10 to 15% of families come forward to donate. This is a paradigm shift,” he observed.

About 72% of deceased organ donations in the country happens in five States - Tamil Nadu, Telangana, Maharashtra, Gujarat and Karnataka. Southern states, he said, have done well in terms of creating awareness on organ donations.

Compared with other States, awareness about organ donation was far higher in Tamil Nadu. Unpublished data from a major transplant centre showed that the acceptance rate was 70 to 75% after the first counselling and increased by another 10% following the second counselling, a senior doctor noted.

“According to me, awareness creation can be approached in two ways. One is to organise awareness campaigns and sessions and encourage people to take pledges. In T.N.’s experience, we found that news about successful donations, honour walks for donors and giving due recognition to donors were more effective awareness tools. Since October 2023 (the former DMK government issued an order to accord State honours to the mortal remains of deceased donors in September 2023), more than 800 such State honours have been accorded. News about successful donations and the utilisation of donated organs has proved to be a more effective way of creating awareness,” Dr. Shroff explained.

What’s needed now

Dr. Amalorpavanathan said that the involvement of people and healthcare professionals along with government support has helped improve organ donation in the State. “Successive governments did their best to take the programme forward. We have well developed infrastructure and doctors who are willing to go the extra mile,” he said.

However, this brings in another perspective. “We have an unacceptable number of brain deaths due to the high number of road traffic accidents. We need to reduce accidents and make roads safe. Developed countries have moved towards Donation after Circulatory Death (DCD), and we should also explore this possibility. In living donor organ transplants, we should promote swap transplants in a big way,” he noted.

At a recent press conference on a heart transplant in a young patient with Dilated Cardiomyopathy, Rajeev Thilak Chellasamy, heart transplant surgeon at SIMS Hospital, Chennai, elaborated on DCD. He noted that India has a long waiting list for transplants, and has traditionally relied on donations following brain death, while DCD was not ethically approved in the country. In DCD, the practice of which has been around for nearly 10 to 15 years, the heart is connected to a perfusion system. DCD numbers have increased in North America. If considered, it is a viable opportunity to increase the pool of donor hearts. The number of people dying while on the waiting list has increased and this needs to be addressed, he said.

Dr. Shroff called for establishing green corridors in hospitals for seamless integration of organ donation processes so that there are no missed opportunities. Similarly, every hospital should have nodal officers in place, he said.

World.title: Parliamentary panel flags nearly 73% students drop out before finishing higher secondary
World.content:
A parliamentary panel has flagged a "drastic decline" in the number of schools and students as education level rises, noting that nearly 73% students drop out before finishing higher secondary.

The recommendation is part of the Tenth Report (Eighteenth Lok Sabha) of the Committee on Estimates (2026-27) on "Budget and Policy aspects for providing Affordable and Quality Education in the Country including Review of Central Board of Secondary Education", presented to Lok Sabha on Wednesday (August 12, 2026).

The committee noted that the number of schools at Secondary and Higher Secondary levels are very less when compared with the number of schools at Primary and Upper Primary levels.

It said as per the Unified District Information System for Education (UDISE) 2024-25, out of the total 10,92,671 schools, including all the government and government aided schools, there are 9,11,032 schools at primary level, 4,12,805 schools at upper primary level, 1,61,808 schools at secondary level, and only 90,866 schools at higher secondary level in the country.

With regard to the number of students enrolled, in primary classes there are 6,18,45,033 students and 4,08,93,978 students in upper primary classes from 6 to 8, which reduces to 2,36,68,220 in secondary, and further reduces to 1,64,17,949 in higher secondary classes.

Drastic decline in number of schools

"The committee are concerned to note this drastic decline in number of schools and students as education levels rises," it said.

"From the above information, the Committee note that out of over 1 million (10 lakhs) government schools, the vast majority are only primary schools, and nearly 73% of students drop out before finishing higher secondary," it added.

The committee strongly urged the Ministry to prioritise upgrading existing primary and secondary schools into full higher secondary schools to ensure a high school is physically accessible to students belonging to different communities and to arrest student drop-off rate.

"The Committee are of the view that there is an urgent need to increase the number of schools at secondary and higher secondary levels," it said.

Considering that education is placed in the Concurrent List of the Constitution with most schools under the jurisdiction of the State Governments and UT Administration, the committee desired the Ministry to impress upon all the State/UT Government to take steps for setting up of more secondary and higher secondary schools so as to increase the enrolment of students in the country.

Gap in the availability of CwSN friendly infrastructure

On facilities for Divyang students to achieve inclusive education across the country, the committee flagged a severe gap in the availability of CwSN friendly infrastructure, noting that more than half of schools across the country are devoid of CwSN-friendly infrastructure.

The committee noted that in order to achieve the objective of inclusive education, the Ministry of Education provides financial support to State Governments and Union Territories to strengthen infrastructure and human resources for inclusive education of Divyang students under the Samagra Shiksha scheme.

To improve physical accessibility of schools, the scheme includes specific provisions for the creation of barrier-free and differently-abled-friendly infrastructure, such as ramps, handrails and accessible toilets, so that children with disabilities can move safely and participate fully in school activities.

Though the committee appreciated the vision of the Ministry, it noted that as per UDISE+ 2024-25, out of total 14,71,437 schools at national level, only 5,23,143 schools have CwSN (Children with special needs) toilets, and only 8,08,466 schools have ramps with handrails.

During 2024-25, a budget of ₹482 lakh was allocated for construction of 186 CwSN toilets, however only ₹2.60 lakh was actually utilised with no progress in physical targets.

"The severe gap in the availability of CwSN friendly infrastructure shows that more than half of the schools across the country are devoid of CwSN friendly infrastructure," the committee said.

The committee further noted that under the financial support for new special educators, only ₹80.50 lakh was utilised against a budgetary grant (elementary section) of ₹962 lakh.

It also noted that a meagre progress was achieved in the area of recruiting/retaining special educators for CwSN students.

On the Ministry's approach to promoting education for Divyang children, the committee noted that it is rights based, inclusive and holistic.

It said The Rights of Persons with Disabilities (RPnD) Act, 2016 provides that children with benchmark disabilities are entitled to free education up to the age of 18 years.

The NEP 2020 emphasises a Zero Rejection Policy for children with disabilities, ensuring that no child is denied schooling on account of disability. The policy also underscores the importance of preparing and training teachers to handle inclusive classrooms effectively, it said.

"In view of the above, the Committee strongly recommend the Ministry to adhere to yearly targets of budget utilisation and execution of CwSN related projects in a time bound manner," it said.

The committee recommended the Ministry provide safe and accessible infrastructure to Divyang students in a time-bound manner to achieve the objective of inclusivity in education.

The Ministry should also assess the requirement of special educators across the country and complete their recruitment at the earliest, it said.

World.title: Justice Yashwant Varma inquiry: What the panel found and what happens next? | Explained
World.content:
The story so far:

The inquiry into Justice Yashwant Varma’s alleged possession of unexplained cash has reached a crucial stage, with a three-member committee appointed by Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla finding all three Articles of Charge against him “proved”. The report was tabled in both Houses on Wednesday (August 12, 2026).

Also read | Delhi High Court Justice Yashwant Varma cash row: timeline of events

The controversy began after a fire at Justice Varma’s official residence at 30, Tughlaq Crescent, New Delhi, on March 14, 2025. Firefighters responding to the blaze found burnt currency notes in a storeroom. Justice Varma, then a Delhi High Court judge, denied ownership of the cash and questioned the manner in which the evidence was handled.

A motion seeking his removal was subsequently signed by nearly 200 MPs. Under the Judges (Inquiry) Act, 1968, the Speaker constituted an inquiry committee headed by Supreme Court judge Justice Aravind Kumar, with Bombay High Court Chief Justice Shree Chandrashekhar and senior advocate B.V. Acharya as members. The committee submitted its report to the Speaker in May.

What did the committee find?

The report identifies three charges.

First, it found that substantial quantities of unexplained ₹500 currency notes were found in a storeroom within Justice Varma’s official residential premises and that he failed to give a satisfactory explanation about their presence, source or ownership. Article I was therefore proved.

Second, the committee found that material evidence was not properly secured or preserved. It held that the evidentiary condition of the storeroom was disturbed before lawful sealing and inspection, and that the subsequent non-availability of the currency remained unexplained.

Third, it examined Justice Varma’s explanations and found them wanting. The report said they did not display the “candour, transparency and institutional responsibility” expected in the circumstances and remained “evasive and unsatisfactory” when tested against independent official witnesses and corroborative material. Article III was proved.

The committee’s consolidated finding is unequivocal: “Articles of Charges I, II and III are proved.” It then submitted the report and inquiry record for “such further action as may be considered in accordance with law”. The findings do not themselves remove a judge from office.

What happens next?

Ordinarily, a finding of proved misbehaviour under Section 6 of the Judges (Inquiry) Act sends the removal motion back to the House in which it is pending, along with the committee’s report. If adopted, the motion must be passed by both Houses with the Constitution’s special majority — a majority of the total membership and at least two-thirds of members present and voting.

The Houses would then present an address to the President seeking removal.

But Justice Varma’s resignation has complicated this route. Though he has resigned, the Allahabad High Court official website continues to mention him as one of the senior-judge most judges of the high court.

His resignation has not been formally notified, although legal commentators have argued that such a resignation takes effect without separate acceptance. Article 217 permits a High Court judge to resign by writing to the President.

If his resignation treated as effective, there is no longer a sitting judge to remove, making the parliamentary process effectively infructuous.

The Judges (Inquiry) Act does not expressly set out a separate punishment after a judge has left office; Section 6 links the committee’s finding of guilt to consideration of the removal motion.

This creates a question over whether Parliament can proceed after resignation. The report does not resolve this issue as its concluding paragraph recommends further action in accordance with law.

Officially, the government has not made a statement, but senior officials have argued that it can proceed with the removal process as the proceedings for it started much before Justice Varma resigned. These officials have argued that the issue is one of fixing accountability and probity in the judiciary. However, there isn’t clarity just yet as to when and how the government would like to proceed with the findings of the three-member panel.

World.title: Gatekeeper dies while trying to save man from being hit by train
World.content:
An attempt made by a railway gatekeeper at Gopurarajapuram near Papanasam in Thanjavur district to save another person from being run over by a train on Wednesday (August 12, 2026) night, cost his life.

Inquiries reveal that the gatekeeper, Rahul Kumar (30) of Keerthai hamlet, Baghpat district, Uttar Pradesh, posted for duty at the level crossing (LC) gate at Gopurarajapuram, saw a person heading towards the railway track while the Nagarcoil-Tambaram Antyodaya train was fast approaching the LC at around 11-45 p.m. on August 12.

Immediately, he ran towards the person and attempted to pull that person to safety. However, in the process, he too was hit by the speeding train and lost his life. The identity of the person whom the railway gatekeeper attempted to save but killed in the accident, was yet to be identified, according to official sources.

World.title: Wild elephant, calf fatally struck by train near Walayar on Kerala-Tamil Nadu border
World.content:
A wild elephant and its calf were killed after being hit by the Mangaluru-Chennai Superfast Express near Puduppathy at Chavadippara on the Walayar-Palakkad forest stretch early on Thursday (August 13, 2026).

The accident occurred around 12.30 a.m. on the Tamil Nadu side of the Kerala-Tamil Nadu border. Both elephants became trapped under the locomotive, disrupting train services for several hours.

Forest officials and the police, including personnel from the Walayar forest range, reached the spot and led efforts to remove the carcasses and clear the track.

A veterinary team from Thrissur, including a veterinary surgeon, reached the site to conduct the post-mortem examination. Forest officials from Tamil Nadu also arrived at the scene.

In February, another elephant was killed after being hit by a train near Walayar.

Trains operating on the stretch at night travel at reduced speeds because of the presence of elephants and other wildlife.

World.title: West Asia war LIVE: Trump 'low-key' bets on economic pressure against Iran
World.content:
Keeping a low profile doesn’t come naturally to Donald Trump.

Yet that is the strategy the American President says he now favors in the war against Iran, and he is betting on economic pressure over diplomacy or new strikes.

Also read | Do not write the obituary of international law yet

“We are low-keying it,” Mr. Trump told news site Axios by phone Sunday (August 9, 2026).

“We’re only semi-negotiating with them. We are just watching Iran with its huge inflation and the fact they have no money.”

Also read | A new security triangle emerges with the Makkah Pact

The billionaire has since repeated that he is keeping the option of striking Tehran on the table, but prefers to stress the economic damage inflicted on the country through economic sanctions.

World.title: Bihar Cabinet gives nod to develop 300 B.Ed. Colleges into multidisciplinary degree colleges
World.content:
The Bihar cabinet on Wednesday (August 12, 2026) gave its nod to develop 300 ‘stand-alone’ private teacher education institutions (B.Ed.) operating in Bihar into multidisciplinary degree colleges.

The decision will add another 300 additional degree colleges which will offer undergraduate programmes in Arts, Science, Commerce, and other disciplines along with teacher education (B.Ed.) and skill-based courses, Cabinet Secretariat Department’s Secretary Mohammad Sohail said in a post cabinet briefing.

The decision was taken in accordance with the National Education Policy (NEP), 2020, and the guidelines of the National Council for Teacher Education (NCTE), he added.

The new academic programmes will be conducted in accordance with the standards and necessary approvals prescribed by the concerned university, UGC, NCTE, and the State government, Mr. Sohail said.

The initiative will provide students with greater opportunities for higher education within their own district or nearby areas, strengthen access to higher education, and contribute to increasing the state’s Gross Enrolment Ratio (GER), he added.

Extension of Schemes

It also gave the higher education department’s proposal to extend the Bihar Student Credit Card Scheme for another five years from 2026-27 to 2030-31, Mr. Sohail said, adding that ₹950 crore has been approved to be spent in the current financial year 2026-27.

Stating 4.15 lakh students have been benefitted from the SCC scheme, he said this decision will provide students in the State with greater opportunities for higher education, strengthen access to higher education, and promote an increase in the State’s Gross Enrolment Ratio (GER).

A step towards connecting Bihar’s youth with new age employment opportunities, the cabinet also extended the period of ‘Kushal Yuva Programme’ from 2026-27 to 2030-31 under ‘Seven Nischay Part-3’.

It approved ₹430.08 crore for imparting training to youth in future skills such as AI, drones, solar, networking, digital marketing, banking, telecom, foreign languages, and entrepreneurship, the Secretary said and added that it will directly create 6,436 employment opportunities and train 2,57,440 lakh youth annually.

Financial Assistance

In another decision, the cabinet also approved an estimated expenditure of ₹1,000 crore for a period of one year under “Pradhan Mantri Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana”, Mr. Sohail said, adding that the State government would give ₹10,000 per kilowatt subject to a maximum of ₹20,000 through DBT as financial assistance to the residential consumers for installing rooftop solar panels.

The State government’s financial assistance will be given in addition to the central government’s share, he added.

It also decided to set up Compressed Biogas (CBG) plants in four municipal corporations of Gaya Ji, Muzaffarpur, Bhagalpur and Biharsharif (Nalanda) for providing a sustainable solution for waste management by converting organic waste into a valuable renewable energy source, Mr. Sohail said.

The government would give 10 acres of land for a period of 25 years to IOCL, HPCL, BPCL and GAIL for the purpose, he said adding that CBG plants process organic waste and convert it into a valuable energy resource, thereby improving waste management.

Restriction lifted

In yet another decision, the cabinet also lifted the restriction imposed on the purchase, sale, and transfer of land in the notified Greenfield Satellite Cities following the final publication of the Development Plan, Mr. Sohail said.

In addition, the Bihar Urban Development Authority will have the power to lift the restriction on the purchase, sale, and transfer of land after the publication of the draft Development Plan.

The cabinet also approved the Youth, Employment and Skill Development Department’s proposal to amend the admission process for the State’s Industrial Training Institutes (ITIs) and to conduct admissions to 50% of the total sanctioned seats in private Industrial Training Institutes (ITIs through the Bihar Combined Entrance Competitive Examination Board (BCECEB), Patna.

A total of 11 decisions were taken at cabinet meeting chaired by Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary on Wednesday (August 12, 2026).

World.title: Taliban support fuels deadlier TTP attacks in Pakistan: UN
World.content:
• Taliban chief reportedly warned outfit to halt attacks or risk losing support

• UN report points to training links involving TTP, BLA, Al Qaeda

• ISIL-K attacks decline in Afghanistan, but increase in Pakistan

ISLAMABAD: The Afg­han Taliban’s continued support for the Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan (TTP) has contributed to a rise in the frequency and lethality of terrorist attacks in Pakistan, even as Kabul has taken some initial steps to rein in the group, according to a UN Security Council-mandated monitoring report.

The report also points to growing operational and facilitation linkages among the TTP, Al Qaeda, Islamic State-Khorasan (ISIL-K) and the Baloch Liberation Army (BLA).

The 38th report of the UN Analytical Support and Sanctions Monitoring Team, covering the period from Dec 16, 2025, to June 9, 2026, said that “cross-border attacks between Pakistan and Afghanistan escalated, provoked by a high number of attacks by Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakis­tan against Pakistan”.

Like previous editions, the report was unequivocal in its assessment of Kabul’s role, saying that “the de facto authorities (Taliban) continued their support to the Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan (TTP), which escalated attacks against Pakistan, provoking military exchanges”.

It noted concern among member states that the continuing conflict could create opportunities for terrorist groups and generate additional security challenges for the region.

Taliban’s dual-track approach

The assessment nevertheless recorded some initial steps by the Taliban authorities to contain the TTP, although these appeared aimed more at managing the group than dismantling its infrastructure.

The report said Afghan authorities had relocated around 2,000 TTP fighters and their families from areas along the Pakistani border to deeper inside Afghanistan in an effort to rein in the group.

It also said Taliban leader Hibatullah Akhundzada had warned the TTP leadership through backchannel communications to halt attacks against Pakistan or risk losing Taliban support.

The developments point to what appears to be a dual-track Taliban approach, continuing to provide the TTP space and support because of shared ideological ties while moving some fighters away from the border to reduce attacks on Pakistan, avoid a major escalation with Islamabad and address growing international concerns.
